The compact model attains lower realized variance than nonlinear-shrinkage and risk-parity benchmarks under aggressive leverage.

entry.title: Evaluating the Impact of Reviewer Guideline Design on LLM-Based Automated Peer Review

author.name: Haowen Li, Yoichi Ishibashi, Masafumi Oyamada

entry.summary: Compares official conference reviewer guidelines against LLM-generated guidelines imitating strong human reviews for automated peer review, finding official criteria produce reviews most consistent with human judgments. Also finds strict rubric enforcement can be counterproductive.

entry.title: PlanCraft: Sketch, Refine, and Furnish for Architect-Inspired Progressive 3D Residential Scene Generation

author.name: Pengyu Zeng, Yuqin Dai, Jun Yin, Ziyang Han, Ng Cheuk Hei, Jing Zhong, Chaoyang Shi, ZhanXiang Jin, Maowei Jiang, Yuxing Han, Shuai Lu

entry.summary: PlanCraft generates 3D residential scenes progressively, mirroring how architects sketch, refine and then furnish, and treats the 2D floor plan as a hard spatial contract rather than an optional intermediate. This avoids the overlapping rooms and implausible proportions produced by systems that delegate layout directly to language models.

entry.title: Calibration-Free 3D Multi-Camera People Tracking for Indoor Environment

author.name: Ponleur Veng (CADT, M-PSI), Dominique Vaufreydaz (LIG, M-PSI), Phutphalla Kong (CADT)

entry.summary: A multi-camera 3D people tracking pipeline that removes the manual calibration bottleneck by inferring geometry directly from video with a geometry-grounded transformer, combined with detection, re-identification, pose estimation and pose-guided 3D lifting. Enables 3D tracking datasets from unconstrained archives.

entry.title: SILICA: Repurposing Diffusion Priors for Joint Glass Segmentation and Depth Estimation

author.name: Tarun R, Anuj Verma, Laksh Nanwani, Sourav Garg, K. Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: SILICA repurposes text-to-image diffusion priors for joint glass segmentation and monocular depth estimation, targeting the systematic failure of depth sensors and domain-specific models on transparent surfaces. It aims for zero-shot generalization to unseen indoor layouts where glass depth annotations are scarce.

entry.title: KANEx: Translating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks' Interpretability to Medical Explainability

author.name: Krithi Shailya, Ananya Lakshmi Ravi, Venkatanathan K. V., Sowmya S. Sundaram, Gokul S. Krishnan, Aditi Anand, Balaraman Ravindran

entry.summary: KANEx leverages the spline-based symbolic transparency of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to generate more faithful textual explanations for chest X-ray classification, rather than layering a vision-language model over an opaque visual backbone. It argues linguistic fluency alone does not resolve model opacity.

entry.title: Moving-Horizon Estimation and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of Cable-Driven Soft Manipulators

author.name: Lingxiao Xun, Haihong Li, Gang Zheng

entry.summary: Develops moving-horizon estimation and nonlinear MPC for cable-driven soft manipulators using reduced Cosserat rod dynamics, with a smooth approximation of the cable tension-slackness complementarity condition. Provides a physics-based, control-oriented alternative to purely data-driven soft robot models.

entry.title: SCOPE and SCION: A Benchmark and an Auditable Reference Pipeline for Schema Induction and Fusion from Text

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Shuhao Hu, Bokun Wang, Rui Chen, Xin Wang, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: SCOPE is a benchmark for inducing schema graphs directly from raw text corpora, normalized from 24 public information-extraction datasets into evaluation-only gold schemas, and SCION is an auditable reference pipeline for schema construction with ontology normalization. The work targets the usually assumed-away upstream step of knowledge graph construction.

entry.title: Tool-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Repair for Securing LLM-Generated C Code

author.name: Vidyut Sriram, Saatvik Pradhan, Suman Saha

entry.summary: Builds an analysis-and-repair loop for LLM-generated C code that combines compiler diagnostics, static analysis and symbolic execution with retrieval of past repair patterns, evaluated on 5,000 embedded-relevant programming tasks. Baselines show compilation failure rates up to 46 percent and security defect rates up to 49 percent, which the pipeline substantially reduces.

entry.title: MosaicJoin: Compact Semantic Sketches for Value-Level Join Discovery

author.name: Grace Fan, Eden Wu, Majid Daliri, Juliana Freire

entry.summary: MosaicJoin introduces compact semantic sketches that approximate value-level comparison for discovering joinable columns in data lakes, aiming to keep fine-grained value alignment accuracy while avoiding the poor scaling of full pairwise value matching. It targets the accuracy-versus-efficiency trade-off between value-level and column-embedding methods.

entry.title: Sparse by Command: Task-Conditional Compute Skipping for Multi-Task Inference Accelerators

author.name: Afzal Ahmad, Gaoyu Mao, Shoubo Hu, Hui-Ling Zhen, Mingxuan Yuan, Xinyu Chen, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper exploits the observation that a multi-task model knows its task command before inference begins, using a jointly trained lightweight gating network to predict per-tile binary execution masks so task-irrelevant output-channel tiles are skipped on an accelerator. Tile granularity matches the accelerator scheduling unit, giving skipping with essentially no overhead.

entry.title: From Isolated Tasks to Structured Capabilities: A Multilayer Taxonomy for Large Language Models

author.name: Shixin Fang (Fudan University), Jiachen Wo (Fudan University), Wenjuan Qin (Fudan University), Sihang Jiang (Fudan University), Yanghua Xiao (Fudan University)

entry.summary: The authors propose a multilayer capability taxonomy for LLM evaluation with 14 domains and 91 subskills organized into primitive, constructed, and integrative layers, grounded in human cognitive science rather than model architecture. They demonstrate utility by screening over 31,000 papers to map benchmark coverage and identify gaps.

entry.title: SiPhy: Single-Image Physical Property Reasoning

author.name: Hoang Le, Joonwoo Kwon, Elkhan Ismayilzada, Yufei Zhang, Zijun Cui

entry.summary: SiPhy infers physical properties such as mass, stiffness, and elasticity from a single RGB image by sampling pseudo-voxel points, extracting CLIP features, and grounding them to material candidates proposed by a vision-language model. A part-based contrastive aggregator enforces region consistency and a heaviness-aware refinement improves volume and thickness estimation.

entry.title: Phylogenetic signal in marine mammal and bird vocalizations captured by audio foundation models: the limited benefit of domain-specific pretraining

author.name: V\'ictor Rinc\'on Yepes

entry.summary: The study probes four pretrained audio models on a task none was trained for, recovering phylogenetic distance between species from vocalizations, and finds strong correlations for cetaceans with general-purpose models such as CLAP and AST. Notably, domain-specific bioacoustic pretraining provides little advantage over general audio foundation models.

entry.title: CausalGate: Causal Importance Distillation for Transformer Module Pruning

author.name: Kiran Nair, Smriti Regmi, Rodrigue Rizk

entry.summary: CausalGate selects transformer modules to skip by intervention rather than correlation, ablating individual attention and MLP sub-layers during calibration and measuring semantic damage as KL divergence of the final logit distribution. The resulting importance hierarchy is distilled into a static gating policy to avoid runtime routing overhead.

entry.title: The Entropic Bound for Transformers: Why Static Rank Fails and Attention-Native Rank Recovers

author.name: Byeong Hoon Yoon

entry.summary: This paper defines an entropic bound as a task-intrinsic spectral capacity for transformers, proving in a linear attention surrogate that the intrinsic rank of the token-mixing operator is a tight lower bound on required capacity and that gradient descent recovers it under low-rank implicit bias. It argues static rank measures fail and an attention-native rank is needed, potentially predicting minimum model size before training.

entry.title: ParasGB: A Graph Benchmark Suite for Parasitic Estimation on AMS Circuits

author.name: Jiajun Zou, Jiawei Liu, Ao Liu, Junnong Tian, Yibin Zhang, Chengjie Liu, Yuxi Wang, Shan Shen, Wenhua Gu, Jun Yang, Wenjian Yu

entry.summary: ParasGB is an open benchmark suite of large heterogeneous RC networks for graph-neural prediction of parasitic capacitance and resistance in analog and mixed-signal circuits before physical layout. Public high-fidelity data has been the bottleneck for reproducible progress in this EDA subfield.

entry.title: Extending Fourier Neural Operators for Modeling Parameterized and Coupled PDEs

author.name: Cheng Jing, Uvini Balasuriya Mudiyanselage, Abhishek Verma, Kallol Bera, Shahid Rauf, Kookjin Lee

entry.summary: The authors extend Fourier neural operators with hypernetwork-based conditioning on physical parameters and systematically explore component designs for coupled multi-variable systems, evaluating on benchmarks including a one-dimensional capacitively coupled plasma problem. The aim is handling parameterized and coupled PDEs with minimal architectural change and preserved FNO efficiency.

entry.title: Latent-LoRA: Compact Latent-Space Adapters with Gradient-Free Routing for Continual Learning

author.name: Reza Rahimi Azghan, Gautham Krishna Gudur, Giulia Pedrielli, Pavan Turaga, Hassan Ghasemzadeh

entry.summary: Latent-LoRA observes that pooled token embeddings from a frozen LLM embedding layer already separate tasks, so it fits a Gaussian mixture in that space to route inputs to per-task low-rank adapters without any trainable gate. This gives task-identity-free continual learning while avoiding the need to protect a router from forgetting.

entry.title: Why does Greedy Search produce Optimal Clustering Outcomes? A Fixed-Core Assignment Theory

author.name: Kai Ming Ting, Kaifeng Zhang, Sanjay Chawla

entry.summary: Provides a fixed-core assignment theory explaining why greedy search in cluster-as-distribution clustering attains optimal-looking outcomes and matches the spectral clustering objective without eigendecomposition. It addresses why distribution-level clustering handles irregular shapes and varying densities better than point-similarity methods.

entry.title: Beyond Error-vs-Discard Characteristic: Toward Stable and Reliable Evaluation for Face Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Bhavesh Wani, \v{Z}iga Babnik, Vitomir \v{S}truc, Philipp Terh\"orst

entry.summary: Identifies fundamental flaws in the Error-versus-Discard protocol used to evaluate face image quality methods, namely test-set divergence and threshold drift, and proposes discard-based variants plus a rank consistency metric evaluated on the full test set at fixed threshold. The aim is comparable and stable FIQA benchmarking.

entry.title: Covariance-Boosted Gaussian Processes for Spatiotemporal Irregularities

author.name: Jeremy Ovadia

entry.summary: Proposes covariance-boosted Gaussian processes that iteratively boost covariance priors to capture nonstationary variability while resisting the overfitting and overconfidence typical of highly parameterized nonstationary GPs. The motivating application is ionospheric modeling for safety-critical satellite navigation augmentation.

entry.title: Gleam: Adaptive Network-Efficient CUDA API Remoting for Cross-Device GPU Sharing over LANs

author.name: Zhihao Xu, Hao Zhong, Zeting Zhou, Yuhang Xu, Haoyu Tong, Wei Wang, Jinshan Chen, Keqiang He, Chong Zhu, Shengzhong Liu, Fan Wu, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: Gleam is a systems framework that lets devices on a local network share GPUs by remoting CUDA API calls, targeting distributed inference across heterogeneous personal devices. It attacks the network bottleneck with automatic model weight caching and contention mitigation rather than raw compute scheduling.

entry.title: Photonic reservoir computing with complex networks

author.name: Sion Park, Kohei Watabe, Satoshi Sunada, Tomoki Yamagami, Atsushi Uchida

entry.summary: Using a spatial light modulator, the authors experimentally study how internal network topology, including small-world and scale-free structures, affects large-scale photonic reservoir computing performance. It is one of the first systematic topology studies for physically implemented optical reservoirs.

entry.title: Constraint-Bound Agnostic Bayesian Optimization: One Model for All Thresholds

author.name: Jin Wang, Xi Lin, Handing Wang

entry.summary: CBA-BO learns a single parametric model mapping constraint thresholds to optimal solutions, so engineers can explore many feasibility-performance tradeoffs without rerunning expensive constrained Bayesian optimization for each threshold. It exploits shared structure across continuously varying constraint bounds.

entry.title: Variational Quantum Conditional Boltzmann Machines for Time-Series Forecasting: Architectures, Symmetric Hyperparameter Evaluation, and a Nonlinear Benchmark

author.name: Gerhard Hellstern, Danyal Maheshwari, Martin Zaefferer, Martin Braun, Tanja D\"ohler

entry.summary: The study compares classical and quantum-classical conditional restricted Boltzmann machine architectures for time-series forecasting, with full derivations of conditional distributions and contrastive divergence gradients. Crucially it enforces symmetric hyperparameter tuning budgets for classical and quantum variants across thirteen structured experiments.

entry.title: Where Quality Breaks in Compressed Short-Text Generation: Staged Bottleneck Localization

author.name: Alexey Gavrilov, Alan-Barsag Gazzaev, Sergey Muravyov

entry.summary: The paper separates two failure modes in compressed short-text generation, codec information loss versus weak latent generation, using a controlled TinyStories setup with a hierarchical VQ-VAE-2 codec and a masked discrete diffusion generator. A staged validation protocol with a shared external scorer localizes where quality actually breaks.

entry.title: ESRVS: Extreme Semi-Supervised Retinal Vessel Segmentation with a Single Annotated Image

author.name: Mingzhi Xu, Yizhe Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a retinal vessel segmentation pipeline that needs only one manually annotated image, using domain-adapted DINOv3 features, multi-granular vessel prototypes, a physics-inspired prior, and adversarial pseudo-label refinement. Reports best Dice and connectivity scores across eight public fundus datasets in the extreme low-label regime.

entry.title: Co-Learning for Missing Arbitrary Modalities in Multi-modal Classification

author.name: Francisco Mena, Dino Ienco, Roberto Interdonato, Cassio F. Dantas, Simon Besnard

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-modal co-learning framework for classification when arbitrary subsets of modalities can be missing at inference without predefined patterns, emphasizing inter-modal knowledge sharing over fusion design. Evaluated in remote sensing style settings where sensor failures and privacy limits are common.

entry.title: Understanding Tone-Dependent Inference Cost in Large Language Models

author.name: Akhil Kumar, Om Dobariya

entry.summary: Measures how seven prompt tones from sycophantic to threatening affect accuracy and output-token consumption on a 570-question MMLU subset across several models. Finds token usage varies by up to about 44 percent across tones while accuracy varies far less, implying tone mainly changes inference cost.

entry.title: You Talkin to Me?: A Network Analysis of Gendered Speaker-Addressee Patterns in Film Screenplays

author.name: Samin Khan, Camilla Griffiths, Shrikanth Narayanan, Dan Jurafsky, Sabyasachee Baruah

entry.summary: Network analysis of 4,600 manually annotated directed dialogue events from 38 screenplays, examining not just who speaks but who is addressed across gender lines. Finds male characters dominate as speakers and addressees even in female-heavy scenes, and that same- versus cross-gender turns differ in how conversational attention diffuses.

entry.title: Explaining BiomedCLIP with Weighted Banzhaf Interactions Supported by Tree-Gram Parsing

author.name: Jakub Rymarski (University of Warsaw, Poland), Adam Rempa{\l}a (University of Warsaw, Poland), Bart{\l}omiej Sobieski (University of Warsaw, Poland), Przemys{\l}aw Biecek (University of Warsaw, Poland)

entry.summary: Improves explanations for the BiomedCLIP vision-language model by using tree-gram parsing to group fragmented subword tokens into coherent clinical concepts before computing weighted Banzhaf interaction attributions. Tackles the noisy attributions caused by tokenizers splitting medical terms.

entry.title: Let Me Look at You: Advanced Facial Expression Modeling for Conversational Speech Synthesis

author.name: Yifan Hu, Shuwei He, Rui Liu, Haizhou Li

entry.summary: FacialTalker conditions conversational speech synthesis on the interlocutor's facial expressions via an action-unit tokenizer feeding an LLM backbone, so generated speech reflects visual affective cues. Also addresses the shortage of conversational datasets pairing speech with video.

entry.title: SHReg: Strictly Rotation-Equivariant Point Cloud Registration via Spherical Harmonics

author.name: Chongjian Wang, Junjie Gao

entry.summary: SHReg builds point cloud registration on irreducible representations of the 3D rotation group via spherical harmonics, giving exact rotation equivariance without fragile local reference frames or heavy augmentation. Intended to fix degradation under unseen rotations.

entry.title: Markerless Motion Capture in Routine Clinical Upper Limb Assessments: Validity and Insights Beyond Ordinal Scoring

author.name: Tim Unger, Olivier Lambercy, Roger Gassert, Andreas R. Luft, R. James Cotton, Chris Easthope Awai

entry.summary: Validates AI-based markerless motion capture embedded in routine clinical upper-limb assessments across 47 sessions with 20 neurological patients, showing accurate biomechanical reconstruction and kinematic metrics that discriminate impairment beyond the subjective ordinal score. Positions kinematics as a more sensitive rehabilitation outcome measure.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of SAM3 for Prompt-Driven Surgical Concept Segmentation

author.name: Changjing Liu, Yiming Huang, Beilei Cui, Liangjing Shao, Long Bai, Yanheng Li, Haoxuan Che, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: Adapts the Segment Anything Model 3 to surgical concept segmentation using low-rank adapters injected into the prompt encoder and decoder, avoiding the full-parameter fine-tuning that prior medical SAM work requires. Addresses the domain gap between surgical and natural imagery.

entry.title: RoadVGGT: Road-Structure-Aware Feed-Forward Road Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Han Jiao, Chen Liu, Jiakai Sun, Zhanjie Zhang, Mengyuan Yang, Yimeng Li, Mofan Zhou, Kun Zhan, Lei Zhao

entry.summary: RoadVGGT reconstructs large-scale road surfaces as compact Gaussian representations in a feed-forward pass using a geometric foundation model with multi-view images, poses, and depth, eliminating per-scene optimization. Aimed at scalable high-definition mapping and driving simulation.

entry.title: Beyond Appearance: A Multi-cue Framework and Large-scale Benchmark for Pedestrian Association and Tracking on Mobile Aerial-Ground Platforms

author.name: Ruiqi Wu, Bingliang Jiao, Ruize Han, Hangzheng Yu, Xunkai Jiang, Shining Wang, Yuanqi Hu, Wenxuan Wang, Peng Wang

entry.summary: Presents FUSION plus a large-scale benchmark for associating and tracking pedestrians across mobile aerial and ground platforms, where frequent viewpoint shifts distort appearance. Adaptively combines viewpoint-invariant cues with appearance features and synchronizes features across views online.

entry.title: Consistent Evidence, Robust Recognition: Faithful Attribution Regularization under Geometric Transformations

author.name: Xianghao Jiao, Ruoyu Chen, Wei Wang, Jiazi Hu, Jiawei Liang, Shangquan Sun, Shiming Liu, Qunli Zhang, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: Regularizes recognition models so attribution maps stay consistent under label-preserving geometric transformations, but only after arguing that gradient-based maps like Grad-CAM are too unfaithful for such supervision to be meaningful. Proposes an annotation-free attribution regularization using more faithful evidence.

entry.title: Multiview Multi-Person Human Mesh Recovery Under Large Scenes with Occlusions

author.name: Qi Zhang, Tao Yu, Jiechao He, Antoni B. Chan, Hui Huang

entry.summary: Introduces MVMP-HMR, a large synthetic benchmark for multiview multi-person human mesh recovery with up to 50 cameras, 30 interacting people, and severe occlusions across 15 scenes. It targets the gap between existing single-view or single-person settings and real large-scene deployment.

entry.title: HistoGPA: A Context-Conditioned Gene-Prior Attention Framework for Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction

author.name: Ziang Liu, Xinhai Chen, Yigui Feng, Shuai Li, Qingyang Zhang, Jie Liu

entry.summary: HistoGPA predicts spatial gene expression from routine H and E histology using slide-level context to modulate both local morphological features and pretrained gene embeddings via cross-attention. The insight is that gene priors should be context-conditioned rather than fixed.

entry.title: Small, Bias-Free, Blind and Convolutional Denoiser: A compact ConvNeXt U-Net for blind Gaussian color-image denoising

author.name: Nikolas Markou

entry.summary: BF-ConvUNeXt is a 0.82M-parameter bias-free ConvNeXt U-Net for blind Gaussian denoising, with a frozen Gabor stem and Laplacian-pyramid skip routing, constructed to be exactly degree-1 homogeneous at inference. That homogeneity licenses a score-function reading of the residual and enables generalization across noise levels from single-level training.

entry.title: A Scale-adaptive Vision Model Links C. elegans Neuronal Morphology to Behavior for Neurotoxicity Assessment

author.name: Haochao Ying, Shenchong Lv, Yutao Sun, Zijian Tu, Xufeng Jin, Yuyang Xu, Yizhe Wang, Wei Yang, Xiaomin Yue, Jian Wu, Peilin Yu

entry.summary: Introduces a self-supervised, scale-adaptive vision model tailored to confocal microscopy of dopaminergic neurons in C. elegans, plus a morphology dataset, to link neuronal damage to behavioral outcomes. The goal is to replace subjective hand-scored neurotoxicity readouts with automated, behaviorally predictive quantification.

entry.title: BC-NMPC: Battery-Constrained NMPC with Propulsion Prediction and Replanning for High-Speed Flight

author.name: Parakh M. Gupta, Matej Mihulka, Matej Novosad, Robert Penicka, Martin Saska

entry.summary: Integrates battery and propulsion models into a nonlinear MPC so a racing drone can predict voltage, current and maximum available thrust in real time and replan as the battery depletes. Addresses tracking degradation and crashes during aggressive flight.

entry.title: SHARE: Towards Head-Mounted AR with User-Centric SLAM in Shared Human-Robot Workspaces

author.name: Tianyuan Du, Tianyi Hu, Hanting Ye, Maria Gorlatova

entry.summary: SHARE is a user-centric multi-agent SLAM system that departs from uniform edge resource allocation by prioritizing the tight latency requirements of head-mounted AR users over those of robots in shared human-robot workspaces. Aims to eliminate lag during AR-mediated manipulation.

entry.title: HELIOS: An LLM-Driven Autonomous Indirect Trajectory Optimization Agent

author.name: An-yi Huang

entry.summary: HELIOS wraps a large language model around indirect low-thrust spacecraft trajectory optimization, letting the system take a natural-language problem statement and autonomously perform Pontryagin symbolic derivations, code generation, and shooting-method solving. It targets three classic pain points: per-constraint transversality derivations, model-specific code rewrites, and initial-guess sensitivity.

entry.title: Anytime-Valid Confirmation of Covariate Balance for Prespecified Corrections

author.name: Seungjin Choi

entry.summary: Provides anytime-valid, time-uniform confidence sequences for checking whether a prespecified covariate-shift correction actually balances a sequential stream of unlabeled target data. Users can monitor continuously and stop adaptively with bounded probability of falsely confirming balance.

entry.title: LC-SEPLM: long-range contact-supervised adaptation for sequence-only protein representation learning

author.name: Chen Wang, Boming Kang, Qinghua Cui

entry.summary: LC-SEPLM adapts the ESM2 protein language model with LoRA plus an auxiliary objective that supervises long-range residue-residue contacts distilled from a large set of predicted structures, while keeping inference sequence-only. The goal is to inject folding-derived spatial structure into representations without requiring structures at test time.

entry.title: Beyond Directed Acyclic Graphs: Causal Zeros and Causal Differential Equations

author.name: Sergei V. Kalinin

entry.summary: This paper argues Pearl's DAG-based structural causal models cannot naturally express symmetric physical or economic constraints such as the ideal gas law or feedback cycles, and introduces causal zeros with an activation operator plus a differential-equation extension where direction emerges only from intervention. It is a conceptual extension of causal formalism toward physics-style constraint systems.

entry.title: Harmonized Interpretable ECG Waveform Features for Robust Cross-Dataset Clinical Prediction

author.name: Jie Lin, Weijie Sun, Sunil V. Kalmady, Anita Khalafbeigi, Abram Hindle, Padma Kaul, Russell Greiner

entry.summary: The authors construct harmonized, interpretable ECG features computed directly from raw waveforms, including morphology, heart-rate variability, and compact time-frequency descriptors, then train gradient-boosted models and test transfer between two large hospital cohorts on heart failure and mortality tasks. The focus is on cross-hospital generalization, where vendor and population differences typically break deep ECG models.

entry.title: Learning to Optimize: Joint Routing and Flow Allocation on Sparse Non-Euclidean Networks

author.name: Haomiao Sun, Fang He, Congyuan Ji, Xindi Tang

entry.summary: DCGA is an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework for joint cyclic routing, cargo flow allocation, and cross-cycle service on sparse non-Euclidean networks, separating reachability and demand-service logic into distinct graph attention channels with a simulator-coupled constraint-informed decoder. It reports state-of-the-art results with seconds-level inference on liner shipping benchmarks.

entry.title: Understanding Machine Unlearning Through the Lens of Mode Connectivity

author.name: Jiali Cheng, Hadi Amiri

entry.summary: Studies machine unlearning through mode connectivity, asking whether unlearned models sit in low-loss basins connected to each other and to retrained models. Across curriculum learning, second-order methods, and different unlearning algorithms, many unlearned models lie in connected basins with smooth retain and forget behavior.

entry.title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems

author.name: Shuo Wang, Fang Xi, Wenyuan Huang, Qing Wang, Junming Su

entry.summary: Identifies a mismatch in which LLM serving flattens richly structured retrieval outputs such as ranked evidence, graph topology, and confidence scores into an undifferentiated token sequence, forcing dense uniform consumption of the whole key-value cache. KAP proposes to make serving aware of that structure so decoding can attend selectively and cut memory traffic.

entry.title: DraftExpert: Expansion-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding for End-Device MoE Inference

author.name: Dengke Han

entry.summary: DraftExpert is an expansion-aware self-speculative decoding scheme for running large mixture-of-experts models on end devices where routed expert weights exceed accelerator memory and must be staged from CPU or flash. It manages the tension between larger draft expert sets improving acceptance and triggering costly extra expert loading during multi-token verification.

entry.title: Visible-Light Imaging Diagnosis of Neutral Particle Emission Tomography in the Tokamak Divertor: An Efficient Transformer-based Surrogate Model

author.name: Xiao Wang, Hao Si, Qiang Chen, Yu-Xiang Zhang, Beihe Zhang, Jianhua Yang, Qingquan Yang, Dengdi Sun, Wanli Lyu, Guosheng Xu, Jin Tang

entry.summary: Delta-InvFormer is a differential-transformer surrogate that predicts two-dimensional light-intensity distributions in a tokamak divertor from consecutive visible-light camera frames, using spatial and temporal differential self-attention. It provides fast plasma emission tomography for fusion diagnostics.

entry.title: LoRA for Gender-Inclusive Rewriting and Activation Steering for Counter-Narrative Generation

author.name: Akhil Rajeev P, Manoj Balaji J

entry.summary: Shared-task system that uses LoRA fine-tuning for gender-inclusive rewriting and a PCA-derived activation steering direction injected into hidden states for counter-narrative generation. Reports competitive official scores while keeping inference-time compute low.

entry.title: Looking for Affect in Spontaneous Finnish Speech through Linguistic Interpretability

author.name: Kalle Lahtinen, Liisa Mustanoja, Okko R\"as\"anen

entry.summary: Systematically compares text-derived and audio-derived features for modeling human valence and arousal judgments in a newly released spontaneous Finnish affective speech corpus. Finds combining modalities improves valence regression and uses linguistic interpretability to characterize what drives perception.

entry.title: A Diagnostic Gap Framework for Evaluating Reconstruction Fidelity in Weakly Supervised Mammography

author.name: Vinceline Bertrand, Ionut Cardei

entry.summary: Proposes a diagnostic gap framework that measures whether clinically relevant decisions and explanations survive the reconstruction stage of weakly supervised mammography pipelines, using a fidelity ladder of three generative reconstructors. Standard image quality metrics are shown to miss whether diagnostic information is preserved.

entry.title: PRISM: Prompt Refinement via Image-grounded Self-rewarding Mechanism for Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Guo Tang, HongJie Luo, Tianxu Wang, Ying Zhang, Hao Wang

entry.summary: PRISM closes the prompt-image feedback loop for text-to-image generation by having a VLM diagnose generated images and self-reward along semantic consistency, aesthetics, and preference alignment to iteratively refine prompts. It aims to learn reusable prompt optimization policies rather than one-off text rewrites.

entry.title: InterOCF: Spatio-Temporal 2D-3D Interaction for Camera-Only 4D Occupancy Forecasting

author.name: Qi Zhang, Xinquan Yu, Kaiyi Zhang, Hui Huang

entry.summary: InterOCF forecasts future 4D semantic occupancy from camera-only multi-view histories by jointly modeling temporal dynamics in 3D voxel space and 2D multi-view segmentation sequences with explicit 2D-3D feature interaction. It targets underexplored spatio-temporal modeling in occupancy forecasting.

entry.title: Metric Surface Reconstruction of Neurosurgical Scenes from Monocular Operating Microscope Images and Microscope Pose

author.name: Thomas Bucher, Didier Neuenschwander, Thomas Petutschnigg, Michael Murek, David Bervini, Andreas Raabe, Manuela Eugster

entry.summary: Evaluates whether metric 3D geometry of neurosurgical exposure can be recovered from standard monocular operating-microscope video plus navigation-derived microscope pose, using a pretrained depth foundation model without fine-tuning. Phantom experiments compare Poisson-reconstructed meshes against reference surfaces.

entry.title: PriSAR: 3D Geometric-Prior-Guided Diffusion for Parameter-Controlled SAR Image Generation

author.name: Fan Zhang, Xuanting Wu, Fei Ma, Qiang Yin, Yuxin Hu

entry.summary: GeoDiff-SAR guides a LoRA-adapted Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium with lightweight multi-bounce ray-tracing priors from 3D models to synthesize SAR views at intermediate azimuths missing from sparse-angle training data. It targets verifiable geometry-aware controllable generation for radar imagery.

entry.title: Patient-Agnostic Synthetic Pretraining for Efficient Patient-Specific Intraoperative 2D/3D Registration

author.name: Minheng Chen, Youyong Kong

entry.summary: Proposes pretraining a 2D/3D registration model on patient-agnostic synthetic radiographs plus spherical similarity learning, so that per-patient fine-tuning becomes cheap instead of requiring training a fresh model per case. Targets intraoperative CT-to-X-ray alignment for image-guided surgery.

entry.title: Limbomorphs

author.name: Alex Alvarez, Michael Levin

entry.summary: Explores creatures called Limbomorphs that emerge from aesthetically evolved spatiotemporal fields in an animated Picbreeder-style platform, probing their species-specific responses to input perturbations. Co-authored by Michael Levin, it blends artificial life with questions about minimal agency in non-standard substrates.

entry.title: Claude Opus 5: Model Welfare

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A detailed review of the model welfare and alignment evaluation results reported for Claude Opus 5, aggregating findings from the model card, automated interviews, task-preference probes, and third-party reports. The author argues the model scores best of recent releases but suspects much of this reflects being an unusually good test-taker rather than deeper change.

entry.title: Spectral Flow Certificates for Depth-Aware Long-Range Propagation in Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Ranjan Veerabhadraswamy, Ajith Jubilson Emerson

entry.summary: Introduces Spectral Flow Certificates, scalar quantities computed from a graph normalized Laplacian that predict, before any training, whether a graph topology plus a chosen message-passing depth can support long-range information flow. The certificate fuses algebraic connectivity with depth to quantify how much of the spectral bottleneck is traversable.

entry.title: FBLayout: Optimizing Memory Layout for Efficient LLM Finetuning on Mobile GPUs

author.name: Kahou Tam, Wei Niu, Yu Bao, Xiaomin Ouyang, Chengzhong Xu, Li Li

entry.summary: FBLayout is a memory-layout-aware framework for fine-tuning transformers on mobile GPUs, co-designing tensor organization so forward and backward passes each get efficient access patterns without costly explicit layout conversions. It targets on-device personalization under tight memory constraints.

entry.title: Agentic Root Cause Analysis through Evidence-Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Amaury Wei, Olga Fink

entry.summary: AgentRCA performs zero-shot root cause analysis for industrial anomalies by combining a data-driven digital twin of normal dynamics with inference-time agentic reasoning that gathers and cites evidence, rather than learning fault-specific mappings from scarce labeled failures. The design targets both the label-scarcity and black-box explanation problems.

entry.title: Generative and multimodal AI for materials prediction and design: Progress, challenges, and perspectives

author.name: Xianyuan Liu, Charles Anjah, Benjamin E. Jolly, Jonathon F. S. Markanday, Joshua Berry, Haolin Wang, Nicola A. Morley, Robert D. J. Oliver, Alexandra J. Ramadan, Delvin Ce Zhang, Katerina A. Christofidou, Haiping Lu

entry.summary: A perspective paper on generative and multimodal AI for materials discovery that introduces a property hierarchy from intrinsic composition-determined properties to processing-dependent performance, in order to distinguish structural, physical and deployment novelty. It argues current AI novelty claims in materials are hard to substantiate without this evidence framing.

entry.title: Data Quality over Capacity: Internalizing Documents into LoRA Adapters for Closed-Book QA

author.name: Joan Figuerola Hurtado

entry.summary: Across roughly 100 LoRA runs on a 4-bit Gemma-4-e4b model, the study bakes document corpora into weights for closed-book QA and finds that once adapter rank clears a hard capacity gate, training-data quality dominates rank, learning rate, and architecture choices. A single curation pass shortening gold answers lifted closed-book accuracy from about 58 to 86 percent on a 15-document corpus.

entry.title: Interventional Score Geometry for Causal Inference

author.name: Mojtaba Eslami

entry.summary: This theory paper notes that geometry built from an observational density and its score field cannot identify causal direction, then develops an interventional analogue in which hard interventions restrict the distribution to a submanifold and the score is defined on the remaining free coordinates. Causal influence is defined via variation of interventional marginals and characterized through derivatives of the marginal interventional score.

entry.title: CEL: Comprehensive Counterfactual Explanations Library and Benchmark

author.name: Oleksii Furman, {\L}ukasz Lenkiewicz, Marcel Musia{\l}ek, Maciej Zi\k{e}ba

entry.summary: CEL is a unified library and benchmark for counterfactual explanation methods, standardizing data splits, predictive models, and metrics across properties such as sparsity, actionability, and plausibility. It aims to make comparisons across the fragmented explainable-AI counterfactual literature objective and reproducible.

entry.title: CARDIAG: A Dense Segment Classification Benchmark of Deep Learning Architectures for Coronary Angiography

author.name: Dominik Bernard Lau, Hubert Malinowski, Jerzy Szyjut, Adam Brzeski, Tomasz Dziubich, Rados{\l}aw Targo\'nski, Tomasz Figatowski, Natalia Zieli\'nska

entry.summary: CARDIAG releases a multi-center, multi-label coronary angiography dataset with SYNTAX class labels, uncertainty and segmentation masks, and evaluates 24 architectures from classic convolutional networks to recent state-space vision models on dense pixel classification. Metrics account for diameter error, overlap, centerline quality, and calibration.

entry.title: Dementia Etiology Diagnosis via Collaborative Meta Knowledge Enhancement

author.name: Siyuan Du, Mengxi Chen, Xinyang Jiang, Zilong Wang, Jiangchao Yao, Dongsheng Li, Ya Zhang, Lili Qiu, Yanfeng Wang

entry.summary: COME is a multi-task framework for diagnosing the underlying cause of dementia across multiple clinical centers, explicitly conditioning on meta information such as site acquisition protocol and which modalities are available to counteract cross-center heterogeneity. It addresses a clinically hard problem where overlapping symptoms and fragmented multi-center data limit AI accuracy.

entry.title: Context-Aware Concept Distillation for Trustworthy Flood Prediction

author.name: Eli Levinkopf, Efrat Morin, Claudia V. Goldman

entry.summary: CACD distills opaque LSTM flood forecasters into hydrology-aware interpretable surrogates by discovering an unsupervised vocabulary of hydrological concepts and using a residual hypernetwork to adapt explanations to context. Developed with domain experts, it targets the accountability requirements of disaster-response decision makers rather than generic local attributions.

entry.title: Generalization bounds and sample complexity for remaining useful life prediction from complete degradation trajectories

author.name: Huy Hoang Le, Kim-Anh Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper develops a sample complexity theory for remaining useful life prediction, giving a distribution-free generalization bound in terms of model complexity and number of failure trajectories plus a matching minimax lower bound showing the rate cannot be improved. It offers practitioners principled guidance on how many run-to-failure examples a target accuracy requires.

entry.title: WISERouter: LLM Routing with Workload Budget Constraint

author.name: Yifei Li, Zihui Gao, Laks V. S. Lakshmanan

entry.summary: WISERouter casts routing queries among LLMs of different cost and capability as a constrained contextual bandit that respects a workload-level rather than per-query budget, avoiding the need for dense supervised data on every query-model pair. It aims to spend the budget adaptively across a stream of heterogeneous queries.

entry.title: SCTA: An Agentic Framework for Stable and Interpretable Target Gene Discovery from Single-Cell RNA Sequencing

author.name: Shuyu Chen, Chen Zhu, Ye Zhang, Yang Li, Qiqi Xie, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: SCTA is an agentic framework for identifying candidate therapeutic target genes from single-cell RNA sequencing, designed around explicit decision points in the analysis pipeline to make results stable and interpretable. It responds to the observation that general-purpose analysis agents produce unstable target hypotheses because of preprocessing and population-selection sensitivity.

entry.title: Variational Boosting for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Pavlos Protopapas, Kaylee Vo

entry.summary: Builds PINN solutions additively as a sequence of small weak learners, each trained so its converged correction satisfies a local orthogonality condition equivalent to a projected functional gradient step. Because the correction networks are tiny, full Newton or conjugate-gradient updates become affordable, mitigating ill-conditioning and spectral bias.

entry.title: When Should Active RAG Retrieve? A Budget-Aware Evaluation of Utility, Calibration, and Cost

author.name: Pin Qian, Su Wang, Chong Peng, Junxian You, Lifei Liu, Haoran Yu, Yihang Chen, Xiaochong Jiang

entry.summary: Points out that comparisons of active retrieval-augmented generation systems are confounded when nominal and realized retrieval budgets differ, so higher accuracy may just reflect more retrieval. It recasts active retrieval as marginal-utility estimation and separates whether trigger scores rank useful retrievals, whether they are calibrated, and what they cost.

entry.title: Constrained Reinforcement Learning Using Successor Representations

author.name: Michael Girstl, Alexander Mattick, Christopher Mutschler

entry.summary: SafeDSR extends deep successor representations to constrained reinforcement learning so that policies can be quickly retrained when the cost or safety constraint changes, as with moving obstacles or domain shift. The decoupling of dynamics features from cost weights is what enables fast adaptation.

entry.title: Every Client Is an Environment: Federated De-confounding for Spatio-Temporal Forecasting

author.name: Qingxiang Liu, Anqi Liang, Heng Wang, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: Reframes cross-client heterogeneity in federated spatio-temporal forecasting as environmental diversity to be exploited rather than noise to be personalized away, treating each client as a distinct environment providing complementary views of one underlying system. It applies de-confounding to learn invariant forecasting mechanisms.

entry.title: BettiSplit: Topology-Guided Privacy-Aware Split Learning Against Feature Inversion and Gradient Leakage

author.name: Akarsh K. Nair, Muhammad Arifur Rahman, David Brown, Mufti Mahmud

entry.summary: BettiSplit uses persistent homology (Betti complexity) of intermediate activations to decide where to cut a network in split learning so that clients leak less through smashed features. The layerwise analysis shows privacy risk jumps sharply at certain depths, with feature inversion reaching very high reconstruction fidelity at deep cut points.

entry.title: Meshless Domain Randomization via Explicit Parameter Perturbation of 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Felipe Nunes Carbone de Carvalho, Joyce de Morais Souza, Alan de Aguiar, Charles Morphy D. Santos, Jo\~ao Paulo Gois

entry.summary: Performs domain randomization directly in the parameter space of 3D Gaussian splatting instead of using polygon meshes, perturbing spherical harmonic coefficients for photometric variation and replacing appearance to isolate geometry. This enables sim-to-real training data for organic subjects like insect specimens that are hard to mesh.

entry.title: WCM: World-Cognition Model for Generalizable Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Yuzhen Chen, KC Zhou

entry.summary: WCM is a human-centered embodied agent that separates sensing, logic, action, and knowledge in an asynchronous runtime so a robot can explain why it chose an action and be corrected or taught mid-task. It contrasts with VLA policies and world-model planners that optimize instruction execution without interaction transparency.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi-Scale Forecasting and Gate-Localized Conformal Prediction for Multivariate Nonstationary Time Series

author.name: Ziling Ma, Junshu Jiang, \'Angel L\'opez-Oriona, Ying Sun, Hernando Ombao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a forecasting framework for nonstationary multivariate time series that mixes horizon-specific temporal experts via a learned gate, then reuses that gate state to localize conformal prediction intervals. Coupling calibration to the predictive regime is meant to give sharper, regime-aware uncertainty bounds.

entry.title: Data-Driven Diffusion Processes on Differential Forms via the Projected Ambient Connection Laplacian

author.name: Alvaro Almeida Gomez, Jorge Duque Franco

entry.summary: The authors extend diffusion maps and vector diffusion maps from scalar functions and vector fields to differential forms of arbitrary degree, building a mesh-free matrix-valued operator estimated directly from point clouds. This gives a data-driven approximation of the projected ambient connection Laplacian on sampled manifolds.

entry.title: FedTaste: Topology-Aware Structural Transfer for Multimodal Federated Learning with Missing Modalities

author.name: Haochen Liang, Jie Zhang, Hideya Ochiai

entry.summary: FedTaste tackles multimodal federated learning when clients are missing modalities by transferring group-level relational structure rather than aligning fragile per-sample features. The approach is parameter-efficient and avoids generative imputation or external auxiliary data.

entry.title: PathRIR: Physics-Guided Acoustic Path Selection and Late-Tail Compensation for Fast Room Impulse Response Simulation

author.name: Shaoheng Xu, Chunyi Sun, Jihui Zhang, Amy Bastine, Prasanga N. Samarasinghe, Thushara D. Abhayapala

entry.summary: PathRIR speeds up image-source-method room impulse response simulation by learning which acoustic reflection paths matter and pruning the rest, then using a small MLP to predict and regenerate the missing late reverberation energy. It preserves physical interpretability while cutting cost on complex 3D rooms.

entry.title: When Every Simulation Counts: Value-Based Reinforcement Learning for Accelerated Photonics Inverse Design

author.name: Longying Wen, Feiyang Wu, Jinglin Yu, Chongxian Yuan, Renjie Li, Zhaoyu Zhang

entry.summary: The authors benchmark baseline DQN plus six value-learning variants for inverse design of photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers under a tight 83-simulation budget, with matched initializations and a shared objective. Dueling DQN emerges as the most reliable under extreme sample scarcity.

entry.title: Distributed Convolutional Rank Regression over Decentralized Networks

author.name: Chunjing Li, Tiange Zhao, Xiaohui Yuan

entry.summary: The paper develops decentralized convolution rank regression over networks, using consensus-constrained optimization with a kernel-smoothed rank loss so nodes share only with neighbors. It establishes finite-sample error bounds and exact support recovery for the sparse LASSO variant, solved with generalized consensus ADMM.

entry.title: Cross-Attention Calibrated Deduplication for Retrieval-Augmented Generation System

author.name: Phuong Le Huy, Nam H. Nguyen, Quan V. Dang

entry.summary: CACD deduplicates RAG chunks using a cross-encoder comparison against a pool of already-retained chunks, preserving token-level interaction rather than collapsing each chunk to a single pooled vector for cosine thresholding. The goal is smaller vector databases and faster retrieval without discarding genuinely distinct near-topic chunks.

entry.title: The balance between compactness and forecast accuracy of data-driven latent-space reduced-order models in controlled wake flows

author.name: Alberto Solera-Rico, Patricia Garc\'ia-Caspue\~nas, Carlos Sanmiguel Vila, Stefano Discetti

entry.summary: Compares POD, convolutional autoencoders, and two variational autoencoder variants as spatial encoders for latent-space reduced-order models of actuated wake flows, then evaluates how well latent coordinates support time-stepping prediction. Highlights a tradeoff between latent compactness and forecast accuracy for real-time flow control.

entry.title: A Model for Imbalanced Label Aggregation: A Focus on Minority-Class Detection

author.name: Gabriel Singer, Samuel Gruffaz, Olivier Vo Van, Nicolas Vayatis, Argyris Kalogeratos

entry.summary: Introduces a generative label-aggregation model for crowdsourcing that jointly captures class-dependent annotator accuracy and item difficulty, targeting settings where the rare minority class matters most. Fills a gap left by prior models that handle one factor but not both.

entry.title: Speech Signals Complement LLMs for Predicting Interpersonal Attraction in Speed Dating

author.name: Yuriko Kikuchi, Takato Hayashi, Ryusei Kimura, Naoya Inoue, Ryo Ishii, Shogo Okada

entry.summary: Tests whether a supervised speech predictor adds information beyond a transcript-only LLM when predicting reported interpersonal attraction in Japanese speed-dating conversations. Finds combining modalities reliably improves pairwise ranking but that per-participant correlation gains are conditional on round and rating dimension.

entry.title: Do Diagrams Help Large Language Models Reason? Evidence from Syllogistic Reasoning

author.name: Risako Ando, Koji Mineshima

entry.summary: Compares natural language, logical notation, linear diagrams, and Euler diagrams as input formats for 285 syllogistic reasoning problems on two older models, finding diagrams do not reliably help. Models handle entailment and contradiction reasonably but fail on neutral cases and commit systematic conversion errors resembling human fallacies.

entry.title: HiTMS: A High-Throughput Multi-Stream Linguistic Steganography Framework

author.name: Ruiyi Yan, Yugo Murawaki, Zhongliang Yang

entry.summary: HiTMS extends generative linguistic steganography from single-stream to multi-stream, spreading a secret across several batched responses over successive interaction rounds to raise throughput while hiding slot occupancy and payload completion. Includes wrapping to ensure recoverability under batched inference.

entry.title: Histopathological Spectrum-Guided Prostate Stratification via Segmentation-Assisted Diagnostic Transformer

author.name: Leyang Li, Lihua Chen, Huangang Hu, Tianhang Hao, Hao Cheng, Xin Zhang, Qianru Sun, Bingxu Lu, Wenlong Yu, Feng Duan

entry.summary: Constructs a prostate cancer histopathology spectrum dataset and reformulates mpMRI assessment as a four-class clinically meaningful classification instead of PI-RADS scoring or binary labels. Proposes a language-guided, segmentation-assisted transformer using zero-shot segmentation for anatomical priors plus multi-modal slice fusion.

entry.title: Post-Operative Glioma Segmentation via Loss Stabilization, Normalization and Subspace Attention

author.name: Alexandru Cri\c{s}an, Diana Borza

entry.summary: Ablation study showing that Generalized Dice Loss is unstable for post-operative glioma segmentation under domain shift, with whole-lesion Dice dropping sharply on an external cohort. Combines brain-masked percentile normalization, voxel-level contrastive learning and a subspace-aware class attention module to recover robustness.

entry.title: Gaze-Anchored Social Net: Decoding Implicit Relations via Joint Modeling

author.name: Yuqi Hou, Zhuo Chen, Han Hu, Je Woo Kim, Jianbo Jiao, Hyung Jin Chang

entry.summary: Proposes ANCHOR, a target-centric framework that jointly models gaze estimation and social relation inference in static multi-person images, arguing social intent drives gaze rather than being a post-hoc label. Aims to replace independent per-person gaze prediction with relational joint modeling.

entry.title: HALLELUAI: A Hallucination-Aware AI System for Ultra-Realistic Image-to-Video Generation at Scale

author.name: Aniket Sakpal, Yang Jiang, Rouzbeh Davoudi, Shayan Hassantabar, Mani Najmabadi

entry.summary: HALLELUAI is a production system that moderates image-to-video generations for aesthetics, motion fidelity, and hallucination risk, then iteratively regenerates failures through prompt refinement and targeted edits. Aimed at scaling quality control for commercial creative video pipelines.

entry.title: mmSimPrior: Learning Simulation Priors for Data-Efficient Real-World Generalizable Radar-Based Human Motion Reconstruction

author.name: Cheng Guo, Qiming Cao, Shengkai Xu, Haoyu Xie, Kaixiang Su, Pu Wang, Hongfei Xue

entry.summary: mmSimPrior pretrains radar-based human motion reconstruction on simulated mmWave data using physics-informed domain randomization, factorizing transferable knowledge into signal, motion, and radar-to-motion mapping priors. Goal is data-efficient generalization to real deployments where paired radar-motion data is scarce.

entry.title: Out-of-Length Scene Text Recognition: A Two-Axis Diagnosis and a Training-Free Fix

author.name: Zobeir Raisi, John Zelek

entry.summary: Diagnoses why scene text recognizers fail on text longer than their 25-character training crops, separating encoder width extrapolation from decoder length extrapolation and showing encoder width dominates. Proposes a training-free fix after showing rotary rescaling and fine-tuning only partially help.

entry.title: GaitFace: A Multimodal Dataset for Long-Range Person Identification

author.name: Alain Komaty, Luis S. Luevano, Vidit Vidit, Anjith George, Zeina Al Amine, S\'ebastien Marcel

entry.summary: Releases GaitFace, a public multimodal dataset of face and gait captured at long range for person identification, motivated by border-control throughput and the restricted access to existing government datasets. Addresses degraded imagery and adverse atmospheric conditions.

entry.title: PathSelect: Sequential Token Selection for Whole Slide Pathology

author.name: Jingzhi Chen, Landi He, Zehong Chen, Peihang Wu, Lijian Xu

entry.summary: PathSelect reframes token pruning for gigapixel whole-slide pathology as a learned sequential selection problem, plugged into a frozen pretrained slide-language model so both the slide encoder and language model stay unchanged. Motivated by the risk that spatial sampling or static pruning discards weak but diagnostic signals.

entry.title: GRAPE: Graduated Routing for Articulated Portrait mesh Estimation

author.name: Yunfei Liu, Lijian Lin, Ye Zhu, Yu Li

entry.summary: GRAPE estimates articulated portrait meshes with graduated routing, addressing the floating-head problem of face-centric morphable models (which conflate head pose with global rotation for lack of neck kinematics) and the weak expressions of body-centric models. Also disentangles jaw articulation from expression blendshapes.

entry.title: A Unified Stereo Geometry Estimation Framework for Disparity and Surface Normal

author.name: Qizhe Wei, Xianda Guo, Shaocong Xu, Hong Li, Runyi Yang, Hao Zhao

entry.summary: GeoStereo couples a feed-forward stereo matching pipeline with a diffusion-based surface-normal branch, using disparity-to-normal initialization and warped left-view conditioning so the two tasks reinforce each other. The goal is more reliable geometry in ill-posed regions where stereo alone fails.

entry.title: MATS: A novel multi-modality multi-task learning framework for 3D perception in autonomous driving

author.name: Junchen Huo, Wanming Hao, Song Wang, Enqing Chen, Shouyi Yang, Guanghui Wang

entry.summary: MATS is a multi-modal multi-task 3D perception framework for driving that replaces a single shared bird's-eye-view map with modality-adaptive fusion and task-specific mixture-of-experts heads. The claim is that one BEV feature map cannot serve detection, segmentation, and other tasks simultaneously.

entry.title: MAViE: A Multi-scale Adaptive Vision Encoder for Fine-grained Visual Perception and Efficient Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Shaofei Lei

entry.summary: MAViE fuses shallow, intermediate, and deep vision transformer features with position-dependent gates and then routes tokens to the language model based on question relevance and information content under an adaptive budget. The goal is fine-grained perception, including text and spatial relations, without long-context latency blowup.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Conditional Denoising Transformer for Modality-Missing RGBT Tracking

author.name: Andong Lu, Ziyi Zha, Jiandong Jin, Shihao Li, Chenglong Li, Jin Tang, Bin Luo

entry.summary: SCDT is a spatio-temporal conditional denoising transformer that unifies handling of missing and complete modalities in RGB-thermal tracking, reconstructing absent modalities and enhancing weak ones using spatial and temporal context. It avoids the brittleness of generating full missing modalities in hard scenarios.

entry.title: Occlusion-Point Reuse for Ray-Traced Ambient Occlusion and Shadow

author.name: Haojie Jin, Fujia Su, Zehui Lin, Chenxiao Hu, Jierui Ren, Yuqing Yuan, Yanchen Zhang, Zhongtao Wang, Yisong Chen, Kangying Cai, Guoping Wang, Sheng Li

entry.summary: Introduces an occlusion-point reuse framework for real-time ray-traced ambient occlusion and area-light shadows that reuses samples in the domain of first-hit occlusion points rather than reusing final shading values. This provides a ray-reuse formulation instead of post-hoc denoising of completed estimates.

entry.title: Codebook Capacity Governs Perceptual Quality Across Resolutions in Hierarchical Discrete Video Compression

author.name: Manikanta Kotthapalli, Banafsheh Rekabdar

entry.summary: A controlled study of hierarchical discrete (VQ-VAE style) video codecs finds that perceptual quality tracks codebook capacity almost log-linearly while being nearly insensitive to spatial resolution. This suggests discrete latent codecs may avoid the resolution-specific retraining needed by continuous-latent learned codecs.

entry.title: Mixing Configurations for Downstream Prediction

author.name: Juntang Wang, Hao Wu, Yihan Wang, Dongmian Zou, Shixin Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Configuration-Mixed Prediction and a plug-in module, MixConfig, that avoids picking a single clustering resolution by extracting the finite set of structurally stable partitions from a frozen embedding and learning per-sample mixing weights over them. It turns an ad hoc hyperparameter choice into a learned, context-aware feature augmentation.

entry.title: Attenuated Heterogeneity in Fixed-Effects Causal Forests, and a Cross-Fitted Correction

author.name: Harry Aytug

entry.summary: Shows that averaging honest leaf-level effects across trees in fixed-effects causal forests systematically compresses estimated treatment-effect heterogeneity toward the mean, and that the usual additive recentering does not fix it. Proposes a cross-fitted correction and benchmarks against a generalized random forest.

entry.title: The true "test" dataset for a generalised task

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Argues that when the intended task is genuinely general, the test set should be drawn from a deliberately different part of the distribution than training, for example training on Python and testing on Java. This reframes generalization evaluation as a test of whether the intended abstraction was learned rather than a narrow proxy.

entry.title: Hidden Boundary Motion in Transformer Optimization: Function-Space Orthogonalization of Affine Weight and Bias Updates

author.name: Zhang Gongyue, Sheng Yixuan, Liu donghan, Wang Zhiyong, Ren Weihong, Liu honghai

entry.summary: The authors observe that when layer inputs have nonzero mean, part of a weight update acts functionally like a bias update, and they decompose gradients into a sample-varying shape component and a shared boundary component. In a small transformer trained from scratch, this hidden bias-like term is a large fraction of the raw weight-gradient norm, suggesting optimizers implicitly conflate two distinct functional changes.

entry.title: Spectral-Aware Analytic Class-Incremental Learning for Long-Tailed Distributions

author.name: Quyen Tran, Hai Nguyen, Quan Dao, Zhuowei Li, Nam Le, Trung Le, Dimitris Metaxas

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses why recursive-least-squares analytic continual learning collapses under long-tailed class-incremental settings, showing tail-class subspaces suffer spectral collapse indistinguishable from noise, and proposes a spectral-aware correction that plain ridge regularization cannot supply. It combines a clear failure analysis with a targeted fix.

entry.title: Finite-Time Analysis of the Natural Policy Gradient in Finite-Horizon Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Asha Barua, Sajad Khodadadian

entry.summary: The paper provides the first finite-time convergence guarantees for exact natural policy gradient in finite-horizon MDPs with known, horizon-dependent dynamics, proving a sublinear rate under constant step size and faster behavior with increasing step sizes. NPG underlies TRPO and PPO, so filling this analytical gap is theoretically relevant.

entry.title: StageGuard: Physiologically Constrained Sleep Staging

author.name: Juntang Wang, Yihan Wang, Hao Wu, Jiayu Gao, Shixin Xu, Dongmian Zou

entry.summary: StageGuard wraps any neural sleep-staging model with physiology-informed structured inference, including a differentiable penalty on implausible transitions, so predicted hypnograms respect known sleep architecture constraints. This matters because epoch-level accuracy can be high while derived clinical endpoints like REM latency and fragmentation are biased by illegal transitions.

entry.title: Learning Reusable Hybrid Motion Priors for Humanoid Locomotion from Motion Imitation

author.name: Valerio Belli (UNIROMA, UCL), Valerio Modugno (UCL), Enrico Mingo Hoffman (HUCEBOT), Fabio Amadio (HUCEBOT)

entry.summary: A three-stage pipeline turns humanoid motion-imitation experts into a reusable hybrid motion prior by distilling them into a frozen proprioceptive encoder plus residual vector-quantized latent structure, which downstream task policies can then reuse. This avoids retraining a bespoke policy and reward for every new locomotion task.

entry.title: Perturbative-NeuSA: A Structured Spectral Framework for Time-Dependent PDEs

author.name: Xianli Zhu, Jia Yin

entry.summary: Perturbative-NeuSA decomposes a time-dependent PDE solution into a cheap low-fidelity background plus a learned high-resolution perturbation, so the network only models unresolved dynamics rather than the entire field. Tests span 2D Burgers, Klein-Gordon, and heterogeneous wave equations.

entry.title: Cortex: Compact Behavior Cloning for Quake with Frozen Visual Features

author.name: Dzmitry Malyshau

entry.summary: Cortex trains an eleven-million-parameter six-layer transformer policy head on frozen DINOv3 features to play Quake from pixels, using a large public behavior-cloning corpus of recorded human play. It quantifies how far pure imitation with no memory or RL can get, training in minutes per epoch on a single consumer GPU.

entry.title: On the Order-Conditional Optimality of Gaffke's Bound

author.name: George Bissias, Erik Learned-Miller

entry.summary: Recasts classical Buehler-style construction of lower confidence bounds in probabilistic terms and proves that Gaffke's bound is optimal for the ordering it induces on the maximum marginal mean of independent nonnegative variables. The framework is intended to be more accessible and extensible than the original formulations.

entry.title: Accuracy potential of visual localization exploiting high-end street-level imagery

author.name: Jonas Meyer, Stephan Nebiker, Pascal Theiler, Norbert Haala

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates the accuracy ceiling of visual localization against survey-grade requirements using precisely georeferenced high-resolution street-level imagery with sub-centimeter ground truth. It contributes both a scalable localization pipeline and a dataset addressing a missing evaluation regime.

entry.title: Frequency-Aware Dual-Stream Learning for Balanced Realism and Fidelity in Electron Microscopy Imaging

author.name: Longmi Gao, Zhengkai Zhao, Pan Gao, Manoranjan Paul

entry.summary: Uses wavelet decomposition to split electron microscopy image restoration into a conditional diffusion branch for realistic low-frequency structure and a transformer branch for faithful high-frequency detail. This dual-stream design targets the trade-off between perceptual realism and quantitative fidelity that causes either over-smoothing or hallucination.

entry.title: A Controlled Visual-Backbone Benchmark for Multimodal Short-Term Solar Irradiance Forecasting

author.name: Oshadha Samarakoon, Dushan Herath, Ishara Ranmandala, Dilshara Herath, Roshan Godaliyadda, Parakrama Ekanayake, Vijitha Herath

entry.summary: A tightly controlled benchmark that holds an entire multimodal solar irradiance forecasting pipeline fixed and varies only the visual backbone, comparing ConvNeXt, Swin, and three Mamba variants. It aims to disentangle backbone contribution from confounded pipeline changes typical in this literature.

entry.title: Quality-Adaptive Multi-UAV 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Workload Redistribution

author.name: Benjamin Sportich, Kenza Boubakri, Olivier Simonin, Alessandro Renzaglia

entry.summary: Proposes a decentralized multi-UAV exploration strategy that adapts viewpoint generation and information gain to a user-specified 3D reconstruction fidelity target using TSDF confidence. Adds two coordination levels including sparse workload redistribution among drones.

entry.title: Development of a Handheld Actuation Mechanism for a Tendon-driven Robotically Steered Guidewire

author.name: Saima Chavenet, Timothy A. Brumfiel, Revanth Konda, Jaydev P. Desai

entry.summary: Describes a handheld actuation device with a compact spooling mechanism that gives clinicians both motorized tip steering and conventional manual control of a tendon-driven robotic guidewire for endovascular procedures. Aims to reduce vessel damage from difficult manual navigation.

entry.title: Transferable Latency Prediction for Fast LLM Screening on Heterogeneous Edge Devices

author.name: Xiaolong Tu, Vinod K. Mishra, Venkat R. Dasari, Anu G. Bourgeois, Haoxin Wang

entry.summary: Presents a runtime-aware latency prediction framework for choosing which LLM to deploy on heterogeneous edge hardware, modeling each request as a hardware-runtime-model-prompt configuration and splitting prefill from decode. It fuses static descriptors with live hardware telemetry through a gated predictor and validates on Pixel phones.

entry.title: Discrete Action Space as a Prerequisite for GRPO Convergence in Small-Model Continuous Control

author.name: Dmytro Filatov, Valentyn Fedorov, Vira Filatova

entry.summary: Reports that GRPO fine-tuning of a 0.5B language model for continuous quadrotor velocity control collapses to the zero action with entropy crashing early in training, and that removing the jerk penalty or KL anchor prevents entropy collapse but still does not enable learning. Replacing the continuous interface with a five-way categorical choice over PID presets makes training converge.

entry.title: Wavelet Phase Diffusion for Structurally and Semantically Consistent Sim-to-Real Translation

author.name: Kaiwen Wang, Frank Bieder, Yinzhe Shen, Carlos Fernandez, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, Omer Sahin Tas

entry.summary: Proposes a wavelet-domain phase-preserving diffusion method for simulation-to-reality image translation that keeps structure and semantics intact while closing the appearance gap. It replaces global Fourier phase preservation, which the authors argue causes ringing and boundary leakage due to global spectral coupling, with spatially localized wavelet phase constraints.

entry.title: DAGForge: Auditable Causal DAG Authoring with Biomedical Literature

author.name: Yi-han Sheu, Michael R. Steigman, Yu Zhou, Bo Wang, Fan-Yu Yen, Jordan W. Smoller

entry.summary: DAGForge is a browser tool for authoring causal directed acyclic graphs in biomedical research, using an LLM to generate pairwise causal judgments grounded in verbatim literature excerpts and assembling them into a constraint-checked graph. Every edge carries confidence, provenance, and a reproducible literature snapshot for expert audit.

entry.title: Control panels to clarify user intent with Large Language Models

author.name: Ben Shneiderman

entry.summary: A short position paper by a prominent HCI researcher proposing visual control panel interfaces for LLMs instead of a blank prompt box, giving users semantic cues about what can be specified. The argument rests on favoring recognition over recall so users can express intent more effectively.

entry.title: Measuring the Dependency Gap: Diagnosing Inter-Column Fidelity in Tabular Generative Models

author.name: Jie Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that popular fidelity metrics for synthetic tabular data are largely blind to inter-column dependency, since a baseline that models every column independently is judged indistinguishable from real data by a logistic-regression classifier two-sample test. The paper proposes a diagnostic that decomposes a stronger gradient-boosted two-sample test into marginal and dependency components.

entry.title: Pixels for Programs? A Cross-Provider Case Study of Input-Token Accounting for Source Code as Text and Images

author.name: Ronak Bhalgami

entry.summary: A reproducible measurement study of how commercial APIs from three major providers count input tokens when source code is submitted as text versus as a compact rendered image, across five languages, nine file lengths and fifteen model aliases. It finds the aliases collapse into roughly five distinct billing signatures, so the aliases are not independent accounting entities.

entry.title: Khondo: A Multimodal Benchmark for Document Packet Splitting of Bangla Forms

author.name: Abu Tyeb Azad, Fahim Ahmed, Ishita Sur Apan, Ezharuddin Jubaer, Sumaiya Karim Katha, Armun Alam, Amin Ahsan Ali, Aman Chadha, Md Mofijul Islam, AKM Mahbubur Rahman

entry.summary: Khondo is the first vision-native, bilingual benchmark for splitting concatenated document packets of Bangladeshi government forms into constituent documents, spanning five shuffling schemes and 14 administrative domains. Zero-shot multimodal LLMs are shown to group pages by source document but struggle with precise boundary and ordering decisions.

entry.title: Multiplicity of Stable Attractors in Disordered Neural Models

author.name: Raffaele Marino, Roberto Livi, Antonio Politi

entry.summary: Using large-deviation statistics and a perturbative expansion in disorder amplitude, the authors estimate how many stable fixed points exist in a disordered neural ordinary differential equation model previously used for computation. They find that at moderate coupling the symmetric gradient case and the asymmetric case, which can in principle host limit cycles and chaos, behave qualitatively alike.

entry.title: IFCLoRA: Topology-Aware Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Wei Zhang, Xinwu Liu, Yihang Cheng

entry.summary: IFCLoRA allocates a fixed LoRA rank budget across transformer modules before fine-tuning begins, building a sparse task-conditioned interaction graph from a small calibration set on the frozen model. Combining a global information-flow topology prior with local gradient sensitivity avoids the memory and compute overhead of adaptive-rank methods that track gradient statistics during training.

entry.title: MineValiCoder: Reliable Code Generation with Test Case Quality Mining and Bipartite Graph-Based Mutual Validation

author.name: Zhen Zhao, Qihang Yang, Feifei Dai, Xiangfang Li, Bo Li

entry.summary: MineValiCoder is a closed-loop test-driven code generation framework that mines test-case quality and uses bipartite-graph mutual validation between candidate programs and candidate tests, so faulty tests do not mislead optimization. It targets settings where only natural-language requirements are available and no human tests exist.

entry.title: FMOPF: Latent Flow Matching with Constraint-Aware Interaction Priors for AC Optimal Power Flow

author.name: Zhilin Huang

entry.summary: FMOPF uses latent flow matching with constraint-aware interaction priors to sample from the distribution of near-optimal AC optimal power flow solutions rather than predicting one dispatch point. This gives grid operators a way to reason about feasible-solution diversity for risk and sensitivity analysis under high renewable penetration.

entry.title: Domain-Prior-Regularized Graph Modeling for Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Youngseok Hwang, Joonsung Kwon, Geonwoo Lee, Hyunwoo Park

entry.summary: DPR-GM improves anomaly detection in small cyber-physical systems by using an LLM to extract directed physical couplings between sensors from design documentation, then regularizing the learned graph toward those priors. This reduces spurious correlations and unstable topologies when labeled anomalies and normal data are scarce.

entry.title: Short-Term Pain for Long-Term Gain: Adaptive Experiment with Post-Commitment Reward Shift

author.name: Puping Jiang, Wei Tang

entry.summary: This paper studies adaptive experimentation where rewards shift after the decision-maker commits to a single option, and proposes an algorithm that reserves part of the experimentation budget to identify the best post-shift arm while minimizing regret in the remainder. It formalizes the tension between short-term performance and long-term commitment value.

entry.title: Sparse Gaussian-Mixture-Model Q-Functions via Hadamard Overparametrization for Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Minh Vu, Konstantinos Slavakis

entry.summary: The paper builds an online off-policy policy iteration method using sparse Gaussian-mixture Q-functions, where Hadamard overparametrization enables smooth-regularized sparsification compatible with Riemannian optimization over the parameter manifold, and experience replay handles distribution mismatch. Sparsity lets the method prune a large initial component pool into an interpretable model.

entry.title: Variational-Ising-Attention (VIA):TailoredAttentionMattersfor Science

author.name: Rui Wang

entry.summary: Variational-Ising-Attention replaces softmax's independence assumption with an Ising-style interacting model, deriving attention weights from learnable pairwise couplings via mean-field variational inference. The argument is that scientific tasks with short contexts benefit from collective rather than item-independent attention.

entry.title: Soft-Constrained Optimization of Latent Space in Variational Autoencoders

author.name: Ye Shi

entry.summary: MS-GPT reframes de novo molecular structure elucidation from tandem mass spectra as querying a molecule-language model with the full spectrum-induced fingerprint posterior rather than a single thresholded fingerprint. This directly targets the train-inference mismatch that hampers fingerprint-then-decode pipelines.

entry.title: A Coulomb Particle Model for Learning Kernel Attention in Transformers

author.name: Masoud Badiei Khuzani, Sharath Honnaiah, Atiq Islam, Alex Cozzi, Abraham Bagherjeiran

entry.summary: Learns the distribution of random features for kernel attention by evolving particles under a Hamiltonian that combines kernel-target alignment with a Coulomb repulsion term, yielding a mean-field McKean-Vlasov description. It is instantiated in linearized transformer attention by first learning the kernel then freezing it.

entry.title: DECAF: De-Clustering for Adaptive Representational Unlearning

author.name: Anjie Le, Can Peng, Hongcheng Guo, J. Alison Noble

entry.summary: Argues that many machine unlearning methods leave residual feature-space cluster structure recoverable by a simple unsupervised clustering attack, and proposes a post-hoc method combining input noise, confidence suppression, and entropy-based output diversification to destroy that structure. It operates only on the forget set for on-demand removal.

entry.title: Joint Flow Matching for Generator-Consistent Classification

author.name: Hayden McAlister, Lech Szymanski

entry.summary: Joint Flow Matching assigns opposite temporal endpoint roles to different variables so that a single continuous normalizing flow yields consistent forward and reverse conditionals of the same joint distribution. This supports a unified discriminative-generative model useful for interpretability.

entry.title: Low-Rank Dependence Decomposition via Accelerated Symmetric Non-negative Matrix Factorization

author.name: Lavinia Ghita, Dhruv Desai, Jake Goldberg, Roman Yokunda Enzmann

entry.summary: A large-scale GPU study of over thirty configurations across seven algorithm families for symmetric non-negative matrix factorization on correlation and tail-dependence matrices, using a trace-identity reformulation that eliminates dense n-by-n intermediates. This pushes feasible problem sizes to a hundred thousand on one GPU and a million with multi-node distribution.

entry.title: DocHRL: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cost-Optimised Document Classification

author.name: Mohammed Yousif, Prabhjot Singh, Arjun Pankajakshan, Madhu Reddiboina

entry.summary: DocHRL uses two-level hierarchical reinforcement learning to route each document to the cheapest adequate classification path, choosing among vision models, LLMs, OCR, and human review. It replaces one-size-fits-all pipelines with per-document cost-aware decisions.

entry.title: FedSLIM: Privacy-Preserving Federated MDL-Based Descriptive Pattern Mining Across Data Silos

author.name: Samar Samir Khalil, Noha S. Tawfik, Marco Spruit

entry.summary: FedSLIM brings minimum-description-length pattern mining into the federated setting, letting parties jointly learn compact descriptive pattern models without pooling raw transaction data. It offers two variants trading off privacy, communication, and optimization fidelity, plus an evaluation setup for federated MDL mining.

entry.title: Approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser for reducing energy consumption

author.name: Tatsuki Ito, Kazutaka Kanno, Satoshi Kawakami, Atsushi Uchida

entry.summary: This study quantizes node states and output weights in a semiconductor-laser reservoir computer to measure the tradeoff between bit precision, sampling frequency, energy use, and chaotic time-series prediction accuracy. It shows approximate computing can preserve accuracy while cutting energy.

entry.title: BHARATI: Morphology-Aware Tokenizers for Classical Indian Languages with Subword Fertility Analysis
