entry.title: Do Pathology Vision-Language Models Truly See Pathology?

author.name: Chengyang Zhang, Wenchuan Zhang, Bo Li, Xinyu Liu, Jiaming Yang, Mengran Li, Chenxun Deng, Jie Chen, Yang Zhang, Wei Ju, Yuhao Yi, Hong Bu, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: This paper questions whether pathology vision-language models truly rely on visual evidence, finding that a strong general model can reach over 53% accuracy on pathology VQA with no image input and that domain training improves accuracy without proportional gains in visual grounding. It exposes weak, diffuse attention and evaluation shortcuts in the field.

entry.title: Inference-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models via Progressive Seed Pruning

author.name: Rogerio Guimaraes, Pietro Perona

entry.summary: Introduces Progressive Seed Pruning, an inference-time scaling method for diffusion and flow-matching models that front-loads exploration by evaluating many seeds early and pruning aggressively under a fixed compute budget, relaxing the constant-memory assumption. It brings language-model-style inference scaling ideas to image generation. The method exploits sensitivity to initial noise seeds.

entry.title: Beyond Episodic Evaluation: Memory Architectural Bottlenecks in Sequential Embodied Question Answering

author.name: Zikui Cai, Kaushal Janga, Tan Dat Dao, Seungjae Lee, Shivin Dass, Mingyo Seo, Kaiyu Yue, Mintong Kang, Nandhu Pillai, Monte Hoover, Aadi Palnitkar, Ruchit Rawal, Ruijie Zheng, Bo Li, Yuke Zhu, Roberto Mart\'in-Mart\'in, Tom Goldstein, Furong Huang

entry.summary: Investigates memory architectural bottlenecks in sequential embodied question answering, showing that episodic evaluation hides failures and that simply preserving memory across queries in a shared scene is insufficient. Authored by a large group including several prominent researchers, it argues real robots must accumulate and selectively reuse information. The work reframes EQA evaluation toward continual settings.

entry.title: Detecting LLM-Generated Tokens in Human--LLM Coauthored Text

author.name: Yangjun Lu, Hongyi Zhou, Fabian Spill, Kai Ye, Chengchun Shi, Jin Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces a token-level method to localize likely LLM-generated spans in mixed human-AI coauthored documents, going beyond document-level classification. It smooths adjacent token detection scores and uses an adaptive Lepski-type bandwidth rule to adapt to local authorship structure.

entry.title: Dropping the Anchor: Statistical Context Summarization for Distributed Systems via Pulsar Attention

author.name: Aryan Sood, Shantanu Acharya

entry.summary: Proposes Pulsar Attention, a distributed long-context attention method that replaces Star Attention's static content-blind anchor block with a small attention-sink prefix plus compact cross-block summaries built from globally rare tokens via a Max-IDF heuristic. It cuts Phase 1 per-GPU FLOPs by up to 3.3x while keeping the KV-cache footprint identical.

entry.title: The Active Ingredient in Muon's Grokking

author.name: Yufeng Wang

entry.summary: Isolates why the Muon optimizer reaches grokking on modular arithmetic faster than AdamW, showing through ablations that the speedup comes from orthogonalization via Newton-Schulz iteration rather than spectral-norm constraints. Mechanistic analysis finds orthogonalizing optimizers generalize at roughly 3x lower spectral norm.

entry.title: Unified Video Dense Prediction from Disjoint Data

author.name: Yihong Sun, Seoung Wug Oh, Jiahui Huang, Bharath Hariharan, Joon-Young Lee

entry.summary: Presents UniD, a unified video model that jointly predicts eight dense scene properties including depth, normals, segmentation, materials, and shading, learned from disjoint domain-specific datasets via lightweight per-task expert distillation into a shared backbone. It avoids requiring fully co-annotated data or costly pseudo-labeling. The work advances unified dense scene understanding.

entry.title: InferenceBench: A Benchmark for Open-Ended LLM Inference Optimization by AI Agents

author.name: Jehyeok Yeon, Ben Rank, Maksym Andriushchenko

entry.summary: Introduces InferenceBench, where an agent must deploy and optimize an OpenAI-compatible inference server on a single H100 within a time budget across prefill, decode, and concurrency scenarios. It aims to test genuine open-ended optimization rather than recall of memorized recipes.

entry.title: Multimodal Pretraining for Generalizable EEG Representation Learning

author.name: Targol Bakhtiarvand, Jugal Kalita, Adham Atyabi

entry.summary: Develops a multimodal EEG foundation model combining a Mamba-based raw-signal encoder, a ViT-style time-frequency encoder, and a lightweight text encoder in a shared embedding space, pretrained with masked modeling and cross-modal objectives. It aims for a generalizable EEG backbone usable across datasets and tasks beyond epilepsy-specific models.

entry.title: Same Dangerous Objective, Opposite Advice: Direct Exposure versus Multi-Agent Mediation

author.name: Linjun Li

entry.summary: Analysis showing that a high-capability model can give safer advice when a dangerous objective is presented directly than when other agents transform and relay it through affect and constraint rewriting. Using an existing frontier model alias, it tests mirrored trade-off profiles and finds a behavioral reversal consistent with the model distrusting raw objectives it can inspect.

entry.title: Moir: Let the Model Direct Its Own Story for Robust Cross-Domain Knowledge Editing

author.name: Jea Kwon, Jiwon Kim, Dong-kyum Kim, Meeyoung Cha

entry.summary: Proposes Moir for robust cross-domain knowledge editing, tracing the collapse of math and coding reasoning after edits to a distributional mismatch where covariance-based editors preserve only their reference corpus subspaces. Moir estimates the post-training-shaped preservation manifold instead of relying on static external corpora like Wikipedia.

entry.title: Progressive Cramming: Reliable Token Compression and What It Reveals

author.name: Dmitrii Tarasov, Timofei Lashukov, Elizaveta Goncharova, Andrey Kuznetsov

entry.summary: Progressive Cramming grows the target prefix token-by-token to determine when learned-embedding token compression fundamentally fails rather than just missing an accuracy threshold. It finds crammed embeddings occupy low-dimensional structure and consistently degrade downstream capability, especially in generative evaluation.

entry.title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages

author.name: Paul Azunre

entry.summary: DONDO is a family of open, permissively licensed w2v-BERT-based speech-recognition models covering 27 language varieties across six African countries, fine-tuned mainly on license-clear read speech from religious texts. It provides base ASR models for many low-resource languages that otherwise lack transcribed audio.

entry.title: Engine-Native Editable 3D World Reconstruction with Objects and Lighting

author.name: Junhao Chen, Xinghao Chen, Henghaofan Zhang, Zihao Qiao, Saining Zhang, Yongzhi Li, Ruqi Huang, Sisi Li, Yimin Sheng, Jianyi Zhu, Hao Zhao

entry.summary: Lumera introduces a benchmark and pipeline for engine-native, light-aware 3D scene reconstruction from a single image, with a large dataset built from UE5 projects providing components, object instances, parametric lights, and camera views. It adapts a VLM to parse object boxes and parametric lights that can be imported into standard engines.

entry.title: Flash EQ-Linear: Accelerating Equivariant Linear Layers via Group-wise Discrete Fourier Transform

author.name: Zhongchen Zhao, Jixin Wang, Qi Xie, Hui Lin, Lei Zhang, Deyu Meng, Zongben Xu

entry.summary: Flash EQ-Linear accelerates equivariant linear layers by recognizing them as circular group-dimension convolutions composed with channel-wise linear transforms, using a group-wise discrete Fourier transform to reduce compute rather than unrolling into dense matrices. It closes the gap where equivariant parameter efficiency did not translate into FLOP savings.

entry.title: NVIDIA-labs OO Agents: Native Python Object-Oriented Agents

author.name: Paul Furgale, Severin Klingler, James Nolan, Matt Staats, Gaia Di Lorenzo, Elisa Martinez Abad, Christian Sch\"uller, Razvan Dinu, Alessio Devoto, Pascal Berard, Gal Kaplun, Elad Sarafian, Riccardo Roveri, Leon Derczynski, Ricardo Silveira Cabral

entry.summary: Presents NVIDIA Object-Oriented Agents, a model-agnostic Python framework where an agent is a Python object: methods are actions, fields are state, docstrings are prompts, and type annotations are contracts, with method bodies of ellipsis completed at runtime by an LLM loop. It unifies agent and software interfaces for testing, tracing, and refactoring.

entry.title: AttriMem: Attribution-Guided Process Feedback for Agent Memory Learning

author.name: Qinfeng Li, Yuntai Bao, Xinyan Yu, Hongze Chen, Wenqi Zhang, Xuhong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces AttriMem, which supplies attribution-guided process feedback for learning agent memory-construction policies, addressing the credit-assignment bottleneck of coarse outcome-level rewards. It identifies which intermediate memory contents actually support the final answer to guide what to store, update, or discard.

entry.title: Differentiable Logic Programming to Mitigate Reasoning Shortcuts in Neurosymbolic Systems

author.name: Akihiro Takemura (National Institute of Informatics, Tokyo, Japan), Katsumi Inoue (National Institute of Informatics, Tokyo, Japan)

entry.summary: Proposes matrix-based differentiable logic programming to mitigate reasoning shortcuts in neurosymbolic systems, targeting both constraint-satisfaction shortcuts and cognition shortcuts from biased data. It introduces a unified encoding of rules and constraints to reduce semantically incorrect concept mappings.

entry.title: MSBraM: A Multi-scale Self-supervised Brain Foundation Model for Hierarchical EEG Dynamics Learning

author.name: Tao Zhou, Jing Han, Lingyu Shu, Zixing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MSBraM, a multi-scale self-supervised brain foundation model that learns hierarchical EEG representations to capture both local neural patterns and long-range dependencies. It uses a two-stage pretraining framework with a multi-scale neural tokenizer discretizing EEG into semantic codes at different temporal resolutions.

entry.title: PATS: Policy-Aware Training Scaffolding for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yipeng Shi, Zhipeng Ma, Yue Wang, Qitai Tan, Yang Li, Peng Chen, Zhengzhou Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes PATS, a policy-centric training paradigm for long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning that reframes reusable skills as an adaptive training scaffold rather than static artifacts. It converts recent rollout groups into evidence cards and adjusts subsequent rollout context based on task-specific evaluation to break repeated failure patterns.

entry.title: Knowledge Injection Exists in MoE? Exploring Expert-Aware Contrast Decoding in MoE for Mitigating LLMs'Hallucinations

author.name: Xinyue Fang, Zhiliang Tian, Zhen Huang, Ziyi Pan, Zhihua Wen, Xi Wang, Quntian Fang, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: Investigates whether contrastive decoding for hallucination mitigation transfers to mixture-of-experts models and finds the usual layer-wise differences vanish in MoEs with shared experts. It proposes an expert-aware contrast decoding method that exploits distinct expert activation patterns in higher layers to reduce hallucinations.

entry.title: Response drift across frontier large language models

author.name: Mohammed Aledhari, Ali Aledhari, Fatimah Aledhari, Gowtham Venkat Eathamokkala, Mohamed Rahouti

entry.summary: Reports a fully-crossed blinded human evaluation where 47 participants assessed 62 multidomain questions across ten frontier LLMs, producing over 29,000 assessments to characterize response drift from expert-validated references. Every model drifts, with eight clustering at an 78-81 percent deviation ceiling and two achieving notably lower deviation.

entry.title: Instruct-FD: Can Your Full-Duplex Speech System Follow Turn-Taking Instructions?

author.name: Yuzhi Tang, Wentao Ma, Xiling Zhao, Ahmad Salimi, Sepehr Harfi Moridani, Dongming Shen, Jixuan Wang, Abdulrahman Abdulrazzag, Murdock Aubry, Yu-Hua Chen, Daniel Lee, Jaewon Lee, Jonah Mackey, Silin Meng, Nicholas Stranges, Chenxu Xiong, Hao Yu, Yi Zhu, Mu Li, Alex Smola

entry.summary: Introduces Instruct-FD, an instruction-conditioned benchmark testing whether full-duplex speech dialogue systems can adapt turn-taking when explicitly instructed, along with a scalable synthetic conversation pipeline and an LLM-based judge. Benchmarking six state-of-the-art full-duplex systems reveals a substantial gap in controllable turn management.

entry.title: Ms. Forcing: Efficient Streaming Video Generation with Multi-Scale Patchification and Attention

author.name: Zekun Li, Xiaoyan Cong, Hongyu Li, Zhiyang Dou, Chuan Guo, Abhay Mittal, Sizhe An, Srinath Sridhar

entry.summary: Ms.Forcing is a streaming video-generation paradigm that adapts spatial patch granularity to each frame state's noise level, assigning coarser patches to noisier states to cut redundancy in rolling-window denoising. It targets real-time, long-horizon interactive video generation.

entry.title: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs

author.name: Suho Yoo, Youngjoon Jang, Hyebin Cho, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: ReMo is a training-free framework that reduces the input token cost of omni-modal LLMs by removing visual tokens whose information already appears in audio or other visual tokens, exploiting the heavy redundancy of visual streams. It aligns audio and video in a common space and replaces object-level tokens to cut inference cost.

entry.title: Scale Up Strategically: Learning Compositional Generalization via Bias-Aware Evaluation and Data Collection for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yu Qi, Zhang Ye, Xinyi Xu, Yuxuan Lu, Amitoj Sandhu, Boce Hu, Haojie Huang, Jonathan Tremblay, Lawson L. S. Wong

entry.summary: Proposes a diagnostic framework that localizes compositional-generalization failures in robot manipulation policies to individual instruction factors like color, verb, and object, introducing Factor Dominance Rate and Hierarchy metrics and using bias-aware data collection. It reveals how fine-tuned policies over-rely on dominant cues as shortcuts. The work targets language-grounded manipulation robustness.

entry.title: Safe and Scalable Multi-Drone Payload Transport via CBF-based Reinforcement Learning with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer

author.name: Jaeyoun Choi, Oswin So, Songyuan Zhang, Cooper Taylor, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: Proposes a control-barrier-function-based reinforcement learning framework for safe and scalable multi-drone cooperative payload transport, using a minimal 2D abstraction and domain randomization over team size to enable zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. It addresses the coupled dynamics of drones, cables, and payloads. From an MIT safe-control group, it targets safety and scalability.

entry.title: FELT: Generating Tactile Signals from Vision for Visuo-Tactile Manipulation

author.name: Zinan Li, Yiyang Ling, Yuming Gu, Binghao Huang, Chenhao Liang, Sharfin Islam, Hisham Bedri, John Chirikjian, Yunzhu Li, Stefanos Nikolaidis, Daniel Seita

entry.summary: Presents FELT, a framework that synthesizes per-finger pressure tactile images from RGB observations using a frozen visual encoder and a lightweight query decoder, reducing the need for scarce tactile-equipped data collection for visuo-tactile manipulation. It respects the physical topology of dual-finger sensing. The work bridges vision and touch.

entry.title: A benchmark study of vision and pathology foundation models for computational pathology

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications benchmark study comparing general vision foundation models against pathology-specific foundation models for computational pathology tasks. The provided content is empty, but the title indicates a systematic evaluation aimed at guiding model selection for medical image analysis.

entry.title: Stochastic Sampling is Epistemically Shallow: The Dimensionality Gap Between Temperature Variation and Model Diversity in LLMs

author.name: Izhar Ali

entry.summary: Argues that temperature sampling of a single model captures far less epistemic structure than an ensemble of distinct models, using a Marchenko-Pastur random-matrix test to separate signal from noise. It finds single-model variation spans essentially one dimension while cross-model ensembles reveal several.

entry.title: Can Generative Recommendation Reach Cold Items? A Temporal Perspective on Semantic-ID Generation

author.name: Jie Peng, Yanping Zheng, Zhewei Zhe, Bin Tong, Guan Wang, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: Studies whether semantic-ID-based generative recommendation can reach cold items under a strict absolute-time temporal protocol that separates seen and unseen targets. Through hit analysis, a coldness taxonomy, and oracle-prefix probing, it diagnoses when and why current SID models can or cannot induce future items with unseen tokens.

entry.title: CultureTalk-ID: A Multi-Task Dialogue Benchmark for Cultural Commonsense in Indonesian Local Languages

author.name: Muhammad Dehan Al Kautsar, Salsabila Pranida, Bilal Elbouardi, Fajri Koto

entry.summary: CultureTalk-ID is a dialogue-based benchmark for cultural commonsense across 11 Indonesian local languages and 13 topics, comprising thousands of native-speaker-curated dialogues with three complementary tasks. It moves cultural evaluation beyond isolated prompts to conversational context where cultural nuance actually appears.

entry.title: ViSTR-Bench: Can MLLMs Reason from Continuous Visual Cues in Dynamic Scenes?

author.name: Han Li, Si Liu, Zehao Huang, Dongxin Lyu, Longfei Xu, Jiahui Fu, Daxin Tian, Yuliang Xiu, Naiyan Wang

entry.summary: ViSTR-Bench evaluates whether multimodal LLMs can reason intuitively from continuous visual cues in dynamic scenes, focusing on spatial-temporal reasoning that existing static or coordinate-heavy benchmarks miss. It systematically probes a capability gap between models and humans.

entry.title: Loss Landscape Topology Reveals Why Simple Baselines are Competitive at 3D Point Cloud Segmentation Under Class Imbalance

author.name: Antonis Savva, Christos Kyrkou, Theocharis Theocharides

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates 11 class-imbalance mitigation methods for 3D point-cloud segmentation and finds standard uniform-weighted cross-entropy is competitive, typically within a few mIoU points of specialized methods. Loss-landscape topology analysis suggests imbalance severity shapes narrow solution basins that explain why simple baselines hold up.

entry.title: Scene Parameter Saliency via Differentiable Light Transport

author.name: Linas Beresna, Eugene Fiume

entry.summary: Observes that differentiable renderers yield a form of gradient-based saliency, called metric saliency maps, where a single reverse-mode pass identifies which scene parameters most influence a rendered-image metric through the physical light-transport process rather than learned weights. It reframes differentiable rendering as an interpretability tool. The idea bridges graphics and attribution methods.

entry.title: Incomplete Prompt Jailbreaks in Large Language Models

author.name: Yeonjea Kim, Bumjin Park, Jaesik Choi

entry.summary: Formalizes incomplete prompt jailbreaks, showing open-weight LLMs delay refusal until sentence termination and can be induced to complete harmful partial prompts. It demonstrates that simple parameter tuning to refuse such prompts fails to generalize across content domains and attractor types.

entry.title: From Scalars to Time Series: Rethinking Implicit Neural Representations for Time-Varying Volumetric Data

author.name: Weihan Zhang, Xuan Zhao, Yenwen Peng, Yuqi Chen, Jun Tao

entry.summary: Reframes implicit neural representations for time-varying volumetric data as spatially indexed time series trained with sequence-level supervision instead of dense coordinate-wise sampling. This reduces the heavy sampling cost and better exploits temporal structure in scientific visualization data.

entry.title: EmoAgent-R1: Towards Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Reinforcement Learning-based Dynamic Agent Specialization

author.name: Lihuang Fang, Yuchen Zou, kebin Jin, Jinghui Qin

entry.summary: Presents EmoAgent-R1, a reinforcement-learning framework that gives a multimodal LLM dynamic agent specialization for multimodal emotion recognition instead of a fixed prompt. It aims to improve emotion reasoning and generalization by adapting to the varying emotional sources in video and language inputs.

entry.title: Expert Behavior Prior Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Gong Gao, Weidong Zhao, Xianhui Liu, Ning Jia

entry.summary: Proposes an Expert Behavior Prior algorithm that improves behavior-prior reinforcement learning by moving beyond static offline datasets whose low diversity and suboptimal trajectories weaken policy priors. It aims to stabilize online training and improve sample efficiency and exploration.

entry.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks

author.name: Mack Nixon, Liam Wright, Yevgeniya Kovalchuk, Alison Fang-Wei Wu, Martin Danka, Andy Boyd, David Bann

entry.summary: Presents an open-source framework for evaluating agentic coding with locally deployable open-weight LLMs on longitudinal data-preparation tasks, motivated by governance rules that forbid sending sensitive research data to cloud models. It provides a curated ground-truth dataset of cleaning scripts from a British cohort study.

entry.title: Break Through the Compression Bottleneck: From Theory to Practice

author.name: Xiusheng Huang, Lu Wang, Yequan Wang, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: Studies how combining low-rank decomposition and quantization interacts for LLM compression, challenging the common assumption that the two methods are orthogonal. It moves from theoretical analysis to practice to break the bottleneck where high compression ratios sharply degrade performance.

entry.title: Answer-then-Edit: Reasoning Skeleton Editing for Anti-Distillation with Preserved Utility

author.name: Fan Li, Mengting Pan, Sijia Xu, Xiaoyang Wang, Chen Chen, Wenjie Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Answer-then-Edit, a reasoning-skeleton editing approach for anti-distillation that generates defensive outputs to hinder unauthorized knowledge distillation of proprietary models while preserving answer accuracy and naturalness. It aims to better balance anti-distillability and utility than internal-perturbation methods.

entry.title: Verifier-First Evaluation of Agentic LLMs for Infrastructure-as-Code Generation

author.name: Mohamed Jouini

entry.summary: A verifier-first empirical study of seven agentic strategies for Terraform infrastructure-as-code generation on a modernized 186-task AWS benchmark with Rego policy checks, separating failures into validate, plan, and policy-evaluation stages. It applies rigorous statistical testing across all pairwise comparisons and reports findings such as active retrieval via ReAct agents improving outcomes.

entry.title: ODeform: Learning Continuous 4D Motion for Shape Deformation with Neural ODEs

author.name: Yordanka Velikova, Mahdi Saleh, Liming Kuang, Benjamin Busam

entry.summary: ODeform extends Neural ODEs to model continuous 4D deformation of 3D objects, encoding point clouds and physical properties into a latent space and solving ODEs over time to produce smooth deformation flows. It targets real-time-friendly, continuous-time modeling versus discrete or physics-simulator approaches.

entry.title: Rethinking Open-World Video Anomaly Detection: Diagnosing Definition Blindness

author.name: Inpyo Song, Jangwon Lee

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses a failure mode called definition blindness in open-world video anomaly detection, where models score well while remaining insensitive to the user-specified definition of abnormality. It decomposes evaluation to reveal that standard metrics are dominated by target-versus-normal separation rather than conditional behavior.

entry.title: FA-LAM: Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for One-Shot 4D Animatable Gaussian Head

author.name: Yingdong Hu, Yisheng He, Yiming Jiang, Zehong Lin, Steven Hoi, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: FA-LAM is a focus-aware large avatar model for one-shot creation of animatable Gaussian heads supporting static 3D and dynamic 4D recovery, addressing noisy attention and reconstruction-animation conflicts identified in prior methods. It introduces symmetry-aware attention regularization to improve full-head generation quality.

entry.title: Show, Don't Tell: Evaluating Spatial Cognition in Generative Pixels Rather Than LLM Text

author.name: Xu Wang, Kaixiang Yao, Miao Pan, Xiaohe Zhou, Xuanyu Liu, Wenqi Zhang, Xuhong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes ProVisE, a protocolized visual evaluation that assesses spatial cognition through generated pixels rather than text or coordinates, addressing the answer-interface mismatch when benchmarking image-generation models. It lets generative models externalize spatial judgments directly in pixel space under shared task semantics with VLMs.

entry.title: Future Rendering $\neq$ Future Surface: A Benchmark and Dataset for Dynamic Surface Reconstruction Beyond the Observed Window

author.name: Yukun Shi, Minglun Gong

entry.summary: Introduces FutureSurf, a diagnostic benchmark and dataset for evaluating dynamic surface reconstruction beyond the observed time window, scoring extracted future geometry by Chamfer distance with falsification controls. It highlights that current methods are only evaluated within observed windows, ignoring deployment needs like AR and anticipatory planning. The benchmark exposes an underexplored evaluation gap.

entry.title: Grasp, Handover, Rotate: Bimanual Object Reorientation via Compositional Diffusion and Energy-Based Optimization

author.name: Wun Lam Yeung, Wenjun Liu, Yui Cheung Yu, Zhengyan Lambo Qin, Qijin She, Heng Li, Ziqi Wang, Ping Tan

entry.summary: Introduces BiCompoDiff, a compositional diffusion and energy-based framework that jointly optimizes grasp selection, handover, regrasp, and motion planning for bimanual object reorientation under multiple constraints by injecting gradient guidance during reverse diffusion. It handles cases where direct placement from the initial grasp is infeasible. The work advances constrained bimanual planning.

entry.title: Challenge: Hand coding weights for efficient sequence memorisation

author.name: Linda Linsefors

entry.summary: An interpretability-oriented experiment that hand-codes single-layer MLP weights to memorize labels for token-pair sequences, finding that memorization capacity scales roughly linearly with parameter count like trained models but with a worse prefactor. The authors issue an open challenge to find more efficient hand-coded constructions to close the gap and better understand how factual lookups are encoded in LLM weights.

entry.title: Robust Critics: Defending LLMs Against Multi-Turn Attacks

author.name: Roman Belaire, Arunesh Sinha, Pradeep Varakantham

entry.summary: Proposes Dialogue Critic Guided Sampling, which infers user intent at each turn of a conversation to defend against gradually-revealed multi-turn attacks rather than treating each turn as independent. It addresses the tension between over-refusing legitimate users and being exploited.

entry.title: Axolotl3D: a Unified Framework for Faithful 3D Shape Completion

author.name: Anita Hu, Maria Shugrina

entry.summary: Axolotl3D is a unified, occlusion-aware 3D generation model that jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud used as a geometric anchor for faithful shape completion. It addresses multi-view, occluded, and editing scenarios that single-view generators cannot handle.

entry.title: HyperImageNet: A Large-Scale High-Spatial Resolution Hyperspectral Imagery Classification Benchmark

author.name: Chuguang Zeng, Jingtao Li, Yinhe Liu, Yanfei Zhong

entry.summary: HyperImageNet is a large-scale high-spatial-resolution hyperspectral benchmark with over 26,000 airborne patches, 224 spectral bands, 138 fine-grained land-cover categories, and pixel-level plus instance-level labels. It supports both semantic and instance segmentation and an open-environment evaluation with a foundation-model baseline.

entry.title: TableVerse: A Large-scale Tabletop Dataset with Real-world Grounded Layouts for Generalizable Manipulation

author.name: Boyuan Wang, Yue Zhang, Xutao Xue, Xueyu Song, Yu Sun

entry.summary: Presents TableVerse, an automated Real2Sim pipeline that reconstructs high-fidelity, physically plausible, simulation-ready tabletop environments from unstructured in-the-wild images rather than hallucinated layouts, to support generalizable manipulation policies. It targets the physical implausibility and clutter gaps of prior synthesis methods. It is a dataset and pipeline contribution.

entry.title: DC-Leap: Training-Free Acceleration of dLLMs via Draft-Guided Contiguous Leaping Decoding

author.name: Yanhua Jiao, Tianyi Wu, Xiaoxi Sun, Yulin Li, HuiLing Zhen, Libo Qin, Baotian Hu, Zhuotao Tian, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DC-Leap, a training-free acceleration method for diffusion LLMs that uses draft-guided contiguous leaping and dynamic causal verification to overcome the joint-probability dependence error that forces conservative confidence thresholds. It enables reliable parallel decoding in the moderate-confidence regime.

entry.title: Beyond Liars' Bench: The Impact of Lie Typology, Depth, and Sparsity on Deception Detection in LLMs

author.name: Amr Moustafa, Max Feser, Florian Mai

entry.summary: Systematically studies how representation depth, probe expressivity, sparsity, and lie typology affect deception detection probes in LLMs, augmenting benchmarks with fabrication, omission, and exaggeration examples across seven probe types. It targets the poor out-of-domain transfer of deception detectors.

entry.title: The Devil is in the Spectrum: Mitigating Representation Collapse in LLMs via Topologically Regularized Side-Path

author.name: Yiheng Tao, Kaiwen Cheng, Yao Lu, Chang Liu, Jie Chen

entry.summary: Attributes long-context degradation in LLMs to representation collapse and identifies two failure modes, homogenization and isolation collapse, via spectral analysis of attention dynamics. It proposes a non-invasive Topologically Regularized Side-Path to balance mixing efficiency and information capacity.

entry.title: ExecuGraph: A Multi-Agent, Execution-Grounded Framework for Reliable Backend Code Synthesis with Large Language Models

author.name: Sai Deekshith Lekkala, Jothi Prabha Appadurai, Rohith Reddy Bellibatlu, Manpreet Singh

entry.summary: Introduces AISE-Bench, a full-cycle annotated benchmark of 1,133 QA pairs for tool-using information seeking over academic knowledge graphs, capturing realistic intent, multi-step API planning, parameter filling, and grounded referenced answers. It targets gaps left by synthetic-template benchmarks.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware LLM Alignment from Inconsistent Human Feedback

author.name: Jingyi Huang, Ruohan Zong, Yujun Feng, Liran Ma, Lanyu Shang, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Reliability-Guided Preference Optimization, an RLHF/DPO extension that estimates annotator reliability and infers latent preferences to avoid overfitting ambiguous, high-disagreement pairs treated identically to consensus pairs. It targets suboptimal alignment from inconsistent human feedback.

entry.title: CANN Bench: Benchmarking Agent Generated Kernels against Real NPU and Algorithmic Limits

author.name: Xue-Jian Gao, Deng Pan, Yueming Su, Jiasheng Li, Bin Du, Fengming Zhu, Chengdi Ma, Junyi Fan, Qichen Liao, Chengqiu Hu, Xinxian Chen, Lingchao Zheng, Jun Li, Jiwei Yang, Yuwei Fan

entry.summary: Introduces CANN Bench, an open benchmark of 53 operators and 1,060 test cases across four difficulty tiers for AI-generated operator code on Huawei's Ascend NPU, with a three-dimensional weighted score for compilation, correctness, and performance. It extends kernel benchmarking beyond CUDA/Triton.

entry.title: AppWorld-UL: Benchmarking Diverse Agent-User Interactions for Tool-Use

author.name: Junzhi Chen, Harsh Trivedi, Jane Pan, Michael JQ Zhang, Tejas Srinivasan, Niranjan Balasubramanian, Ashish Sabharwal

entry.summary: Introduces AppWorld-UL, a user-in-the-loop benchmark of 516 tasks requiring diverse agent-user interactions such as clarification, confirmation, and infeasibility reporting across nine simulated stateful apps. It extends AppWorld to capture interaction diversity missing from prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Refusal-Gated Decoding: Preserving Refusal Behavior Under High-Temperature Sampling

author.name: Phillip Howard, Xin Su, Allen Roush, Manikandan Ravikiran, Amir Abdullah

entry.summary: Proposes Refusal-Gated Decoding to preserve refusal behavior under high-temperature sampling, addressing that raising entropy for diversity also weakens guardrails and reduces refusal of harmful prompts. It aims to retain diversity benefits while maintaining safety.

entry.title: Code Monitor Red Teaming for Public-Test-Passing Code

author.name: Junchi Liao, Jiawen Deng, Fuji Ren

entry.summary: Introduces Code Monitor Red Teaming, a protocol testing whether a weaker LLM verifier can catch residual hidden bugs after code passes public tests, instantiated as CodeMonitorBench across function-level, data-science, and workflow code. Across 71,000 candidates, weak verifiers improve with scaffolding but still miss most hidden bugs.

entry.title: OPOD: On-Policy Omni Distillation

author.name: Tong Zhao, Yuyang Hu, Reed Li, Yu Lu, Haibo Shi, Yutao Zhu, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Proposes On-Policy Omni Distillation, which routes each student response to the matching text, image, or audio teacher so an omni-modal student learns from modality-appropriate guidance without competing signals degrading other modalities. It addresses the difficulty of jointly improving all modalities in one model.

entry.title: Beyond Independent Optimization: Compression, MoE Routing, and Quantization Interactions in Multimodal Edge Intelligence

author.name: Jay Gor, Karm Dave, Akshita Abrol, Rajesh Gupta, Sudeep Tanwar, Zhengkui Wang

entry.summary: A survey arguing that visual token compression, MoE routing, KV-cache optimization, and low-bit quantization for multimodal LLMs interact and cannot be optimized independently. It reviews efficiency techniques and hardware-aware benchmarking for edge deployment of vision-language models.

entry.title: Workflow-Localized Mechanism Learning: Attribution-Guided Repair and Knowledge Reuse for Structured Agent Skills

author.name: Zibin Lin, Shengli Zhang, Taotao Wang, Yihan Xia, Deen Ma, Guofu Liao

entry.summary: Proposes Workflow-Localized Mechanism Learning to jointly localize where an agent workflow fails, which mechanism caused it, and how to reuse third-party skill knowledge with bounded patches. It routes single-mechanism defects and cross-mechanism relational defects to different repair resources.

entry.title: Reexamining zero-shot summarization: Empirical investigation of trustworthiness of LLM-summarizers

author.name: Vasudha Bhatnagar, Purnima Bindal, Vikas Kumar, Raj Kumari Bahl

entry.summary: Proposes a two-level diagnostic protocol that benchmarks LLM summarizers by the stability of their outputs across repeated generations, at both document and corpus levels. It targets trustworthiness concerns from stochastic variability in zero-shot summaries used in educational settings.

entry.title: BasketEvent: Understanding Who Did What and When in Basketball Videos

author.name: Yu Zhang, Jiayuan Rao, Haoning Wu, Weidi Xie

entry.summary: Introduces BasketEvent, a player-centric basketball event-understanding dataset from real NBA broadcasts where event labels are grounded to responsible players, with a manually annotated subset providing precise event intervals. It targets jointly answering who did what and when, which existing methods treat as isolated tasks.

entry.title: An LLM-Driven Workflow for Automated Process Control Strategy Generation and Tuning from Dynamic Process Models

author.name: Ari Luna Rueda, Eike Cramer, Klaus Hellgardt, Mehmet Mercang\"oz

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-driven workflow that decomposes automated multivariable control design into constrained code-generation steps, from plant-interface construction through MV-CV pairing to Bayesian-optimization tuning, with validation and repair between steps. It is demonstrated on a nonlinear gas-preheater benchmark.

entry.title: Regulating autonomous and agentic AI

author.name: Chris Reed, Alex Austria, Anmol Bharuka, Pragnitha Mandava, Khushiya Mujawar, Luka Shakhkulashvili

entry.summary: A legal-regulatory analysis arguing that governing activities using autonomous and agentic AI breaks standard assumptions about regulatee knowledge and control, requiring the AI supply chain to be brought into scope. It examines four regulatory systems including data protection, UK financial services, and the EU AI Act.

entry.title: Euclid-MCP: A Model Context Protocol Server for Deterministic Logical Reasoning via Prolog

author.name: Bartolomeo Bogliolo

entry.summary: Presents Euclid-MCP, an open-source Model Context Protocol server that provides deterministic logical reasoning via SWI-Prolog for tool-augmented agents. It introduces Euclid-IR, an engine-agnostic, human-readable intermediate representation for Horn-clause logic that LLMs can generate and compile to Prolog backends.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap Between Plausibility and Admissibility: Constraint-Aware Flow Maps for Dynamic Graph Systems

author.name: Michael Romei de Socio, Gian Luca Pozzato, Alessio Merlo

entry.summary: Proposes SeeExplainer, a parameter-free GNN explainer that decomposes a graph into variable-size granular-balls to capture synergistic edge effects that per-edge perturbation methods ignore. It aims to produce more faithful instance-level explanations of graph neural network decisions.

entry.title: Agent-Guided Relational Concept Discovery: Toward Interpretable Surgical Margin Assessment

author.name: Nooshin Maghsoodi, Amoon Jamzad, Robert Policelli, Mohammad Farahmand, Dilakshan Srikanthan, Martin Kaufmann, Kevin Y. M. Ren, Shaila Merchant, Sonal Varma, Ross Walker, Doug McKay, John Rudan, Gabor Fichtinger, Parvin Mousavi

entry.summary: Proposes an agent-guided relational concept discovery approach for interpretable surgical margin assessment from mass spectrometry data, addressing poor generalization to operating-room conditions and the black-box nature of deep models. It maps noisy raw spectra to human-understandable concepts to improve trust and improvability.

entry.title: More Is Not More: What Matters for Diversity in LLM Opinions?

author.name: Qiyang Yao

entry.summary: Uses a factorial experiment to separate two intervention dimensions (input conditioning and others) affecting the diversity of LLM-simulated human opinions, addressing systematic opinion homogenization. It aims to move beyond fragmented, incomparable diversity interventions toward a more scientific attribution of what actually increases diversity.

entry.title: LLM-INSTRUCT at UZH Shared Task 2026: Constraint-Aware Retrieval and Selective Debate for Paragraph-Level Argument Mining

author.name: Phuong Huu Vu Tran, Long Minh Vo, Son Nguyen Minh Le, Hoang Van

entry.summary: Describes LLM-INSTRUCT, the winning system at the ArgMining 2026 UZH shared task for paragraph-level argument mining in UN and UNESCO resolutions using only open-weight models up to 8B parameters. It frames the task as constrained structured prediction with metadata-aware retrieval, constrained decoding, and a selective three-agent debate branch for uncertain cases.

entry.title: Learn2Zinc: Fine-tuning Small Language Models for Text-to-Model Translation in MiniZinc

author.name: Serdar Kadioglu, Karthik Uppuluri

entry.summary: Investigates fine-tuning small language models (0.6B to 20B) to translate natural-language problem descriptions into MiniZinc constraint models, finding that syntax errors dominate failures with near-zero out-of-the-box accuracy. It proposes a cross-model error-bootstrapping approach that collects syntax errors from multiple LLMs to improve generation.

entry.title: THOR: A Theta-Gamma Hierarchical Oscillatory Reasoning Framework for Multi-hop QA

author.name: Ziyang Ling, Ronald X. Xu, Mingzhai Sun

entry.summary: Introduces THOR, a brain-inspired theta-gamma hierarchical oscillatory reasoning framework for multi-hop question answering that decouples global planning from local retrieval and adds a verification-and-repair mechanism. It targets attention decay across long reasoning chains and error accumulation across hops.

entry.title: PrefReward: Learning User Preference Matrix for Personalized Text Generation

author.name: Yue Wu, Chengbing Wang, Yimeng Bai, Xiaoyan Zhao, Yang Zhang, Fuli Feng

entry.summary: PrefReward models user stylistic preferences as an explicit structured matrix and injects it as a reward signal during decoding to steer personalized text generation. The explicit representation aims to improve interpretability and long-context handling compared with implicit parameter-based personalization.

entry.title: 3D-GIMP: When 3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets PatchMatch

author.name: Xuening Tian, Dieter Schmalstieg, Shohei Mori

entry.summary: 3D-GIMP performs high-fidelity object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting by doing a single generative inpainting on a reference view and then propagating appearance with a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm, avoiding costly per-view diffusion. This reduces multi-view inconsistency and hallucination drift while preserving sharp detail.

entry.title: SubSplat: High-Resolution Pixel-aligned 3DGS via Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterization

author.name: Jiun Lee, Jaekwang Kim, Sangmin Lee

entry.summary: SubSplat introduces a Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer that subdivides primary Gaussians into finer primitives to restore structural density from low-resolution features, avoiding the quadratic cost of high-resolution inputs in pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting. It aims for high-resolution novel-view synthesis without prohibitive compute.

entry.title: WhereEdit: Mask-aware Local Latent Editing for One-Step Image Editing

author.name: Ming Hu, Mingyu Dou, Jianfu Yin, Miaomiao Zhang, Cong Hu, Yao Wang, Bingliang Hu, Quan Wang

entry.summary: WhereEdit tackles one-step text-to-image editing with explicit spatial control, identifying challenges of discovering editable regions and achieving stable localized semantic changes. It proposes mask-aware local latent editing to avoid the global semantic spillover seen in existing one-step editors.

entry.title: Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge

author.name: Abhijeet Narang, Kartik Kuckreja, Shreya Ghosh, Muhammad Haris Khan, Usman Tariq, Jianfei Cai, Abhinav Dhall

entry.summary: This paper describes the Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026, built on the million-scale XPlainVerse benchmark, requiring both a real/fake label and grounded natural-language explanations. It pushes the field beyond binary classification toward interpretable, evidence-based verification.

entry.title: WAT3R: Feedforward Underwater 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Jiayi Xu, Jiahao Lu, Ziqiang Zheng, Yihao Tan, Yaolong Zhu, Yuan Liu, Sai-Kit Yeung

entry.summary: WAT3R is a feedforward framework that reconstructs 3D scenes directly from underwater images in a single forward pass, treating degradation adaptation as a geometry-constrained process with a lightweight neural adaptation module. It outputs pixel-aligned 3D point maps and camera poses despite light attenuation and backscattering.

entry.title: GroupVideo: Multi-Identity Customized Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Xinyang Song, Libin Wang, Jianxin Sun, Qi Li, Dandan Zheng, JingDong Chen, Zhenan Sun

entry.summary: GroupVideo generates multi-identity customized videos from multiple individual photographs using video diffusion transformers with multimodal identity alignment to avoid the copy-paste artifacts and identity confusion of naive concatenation. It introduces explicit identity separation for natural multi-person motion.

entry.title: C-PTQ: Fisher-weighted Channel-wise Sensitivity for Post-training Quantization of MLLMs

author.name: Jiameng Li, Han Zhou, Matthew B. Blaschko

entry.summary: C-PTQ introduces Fisher-weighted channel-wise sensitivity for post-training quantization of multimodal LLMs, arguing that existing modality- or token-level metrics fail to capture channel impacts on task-specific loss. It uses task-loss-aligned importance to better protect salient outlier channels during compression.

entry.title: Geo3R: Mitigating Spatial Reasoning Hallucination in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Mingyu Wang, Weilin Jin, Wenbo Li, Haoyang Huang, Tong Jia, Ying Li

entry.summary: Geo3R targets spatial-reasoning hallucination in multimodal LLMs, defining it as a subcategory of relation hallucination caused by insufficient 3D structure modeling that existing mitigations miss. It aims to bridge the gap between 2D visual representations and 3D spatial reality to reduce contradictory spatial judgments.

entry.title: HalluScope: Fine-grained Hallucination Diagnosis for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Weilin Jin, Mingyu Wang, Wenbo Li, Haoyang Huang, Yifan Wu, Ying Li, Gang Huang, Zhonghai Wu

entry.summary: HalluScope proposes a unified fine-grained hallucination diagnosis task for multimodal LLMs that jointly performs detection, classification, and interpretable explanation generation, with an automated data-generation pipeline. It aims to provide richer diagnostic information than coarse-grained detection for downstream mitigation.

entry.title: Detectors Learn the Wrong Thing: Shortcut-Resistant Adversarial Training Against Physically Realizable Attacks

author.name: Yuanhao Huang, Yilong Ren, Jinlei Wang, Xuesong Bai, Zheng Zhang, Haiyang Yu

entry.summary: InsCAT is an instance-level contrastive adversarial-training framework that counters a patch-texture shortcut in which detectors learn to treat adversarial texture itself as evidence of object presence. It aims to improve robustness and cross-attack generalization against physically realizable attacks in safety-critical perception systems.

entry.title: SlerpFlow: Spherical Trajectory Correction for Rectified Flow Inversion

author.name: Wenbin Duan, Yan Shu, Zhuoyuan Fu, Fangmin Zhao, Yan Li, Yaru Zhao, Binyang Li

entry.summary: SlerpFlow is a zero-shot spherical trajectory-correction method for rectified-flow (FLUX) inversion that uses a geometric manifold-hypothesis view instead of high-order Taylor expansions to reduce discretization errors during image-to-noise inversion. It enables faster, more faithful reconstruction and editing.

entry.title: Incremental Optimal Assignment for Real-Time Crowd Tracking

author.name: Ismail H. Toroslu

entry.summary: Presents an incremental assignment algorithm for multi-object tracking that exploits the block-sparse structure of crowd cost matrices to compute the exact Hungarian-optimal solution more efficiently by adding one person at a time. It targets the cubic-time bottleneck in dense crowd tracking. The work is a solid algorithmic optimization for real-time systems.

entry.title: Towards Privacy-Preserving Federated Prompt Tuning under Data Heterogeneity: A Subspace-Decomposed Expert Approach

author.name: Yuhua Wang, Xiaodong Li, Yihao Guo, Yuxiang Jia, Qinnan Zhang, Yifan Sun, Hainan Zhang, Yongxin Tong, Zhiming Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes FedSEPT, a privacy-preserving federated prompt tuning method for vision-language models that uses subspace-decomposed multi-expert prompts to balance personalization and generalization under differential privacy and data heterogeneity. It tries to reduce DP noise and communication cost while preserving diverse transferable knowledge. The work sits at the intersection of federated learning and prompt tuning.

entry.title: Recurrent Sinusoidal INRs for Efficient High-Fidelity Representation

author.name: Hyunmin Cho, Jaejun Yoo, Kyong Hwan Jin

entry.summary: Studies sinusoidal recurrence as an iterative mechanism for spectral enrichment in implicit neural representations, providing a harmonic-line-spectrum analysis of how recurrent unrolling extends effective spectral support. A shared sinusoidal block iteratively refines the latent to achieve higher fidelity than feed-forward INRs. The work offers both a spectral account and an efficient architecture.

entry.title: Distributed Model-Based Diffusion For Scalable Multi-Robot Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Haejoon Lee, Xinyi Wang, Taekyung Kim, Dimitra Panagou

entry.summary: Introduces Distributed Model-Based Diffusion, extending sampling-based trajectory optimization to multi-robot systems by decomposing the reverse diffusion process into local computations in a server-robot framework, avoiding the centralized high-dimensional curse of dimensionality and global data access. It targets scalable trajectory optimization in non-convex, non-differentiable environments. The work advances distributed diffusion planning.

entry.title: FORGE-plus: Force-Budgeted Recovery for Contact-Rich Assembly with a Frozen LLM Supervisor

author.name: Kyupaeck Jeff Rah, Midum Oh

entry.summary: Proposes FORGE-plus, a two-layer framework for contact-rich assembly in which a frozen text-only LLM assigns per-object force ceilings and selects recovery maneuvers from a fixed menu using compact textual force signatures, while a low-level controller strictly enforces the force limit. The LLM never directly controls force. It explores LLM supervision of force-conditioned RL.

entry.title: [Paper] Stringological sequence prediction II

author.name: Vanessa Kosoy

entry.summary: A theoretical paper extending prior work on sequence prediction algorithms tied to stringological word-complexity measures, presenting an efficient predictor for right-to-left automaticity and a new arithmetic repetition complexity measure applicable to mix-automatic sequences. It connects to the author's broader agent-foundations program on compositional learning and control-theoretic complexity for polytope MDPs.

entry.title: Safeguards for Speech2Speech LLM-Assistants: A Case Study in Automotive Applications

author.name: Gregor Endler, Sebastian Kraus, Lukas Stappen

entry.summary: Studies guardrails for end-to-end speech-to-speech assistants in automotive settings, comparing transcript-based and tool-based safeguard strategies. It empirically shows both add prohibitive latency and have technical limitations, concluding neither is adequate for most industrial deployments.

entry.title: Towards Faithful Graph Explanations with Synergistic Edge Effects via Granular Balls

author.name: Jiancu Chen, Shuyin Xia, Guan Wang, Degang Chen, Fan Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SPORD, a simulation-propose-then-OR-dispose approach for e-commerce supply-chain planning that unifies fragmented planning tasks while addressing combinatorial intractability and executive trust. It combines simulation-based proposal generation with operations-research disposal to produce verifiable, implementable plans.

entry.title: A Knowledge-Injection Framework for Zero-Shot Adaptation of LLMs to Delirium Prediction

author.name: Jessica Sena, Shesadree Priyadarshani, Miguel Contreras, Bharat Gandhi, Scott Siegel, Subhash Nerella, Parisa Rashidi

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight knowledge-injection framework for zero-shot ICU delirium prediction that augments a deterministic natural-language summary of structured EHR data with an external clinical knowledge report at inference time, without fine-tuning or retrieval. On MIMIC-IV admissions it improves AUROC by about 8.6 points for an 8B model and 2 points for a 70B model.

entry.title: A Unified Moral-Value Dataset for Instruction Tuning

author.name: Zhaohui Zeng, Florian Mai

entry.summary: The authors merge existing moral-value datasets into a unified instruction-response corpus for instruction tuning aimed at value alignment. They report training gains on moral-scenario tasks, positioning the resource as a direct tool for aligning models to human values.

entry.title: When Trivia Is Not Trivial: Everyday Knowledge Failures in Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Anna Mosolova, Djam\'e Seddah

entry.summary: TriviaRoomQA is a multilingual benchmark of parallel multiple-choice questions across 288 everyday and long-tail topics in six European languages plus a large French-only set, used to test 30 open-weight LLMs. It probes culturally grounded and niche knowledge that mainstream benchmarks often overlook.

entry.title: Agentic Designer: Progressive Multi-Agent Collaboration for Structure-Aware Interior Layout Generation

author.name: Zhijing Yang, Haocheng Lin, Zhihua Xu, Haojie Li, Keze Wang, Liang Lin, Tianshui Chen

entry.summary: Agentic Designer formulates structure-aware interior layout generation as an iterative, constraint-verified multi-agent decision process, decomposing synthesis into modular steps with intermediate geometric checks. It targets collision-free, functionally feasible furniture arrangements that one-shot diffusion or LLM methods often violate.

entry.title: GrainGS: Gradient-Decoupled Gaussian Splatting for Efficient Dynamic Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Jiahao He, Yihua Shao, Zhengkai Zhao, Pan Gao, Fei Ma, Jingcai Guo, Hao Tang, Nicu Sebe, Qi Tian

entry.summary: Introduces GrainGS, a dynamic Gaussian Splatting framework combining a hierarchical anchor scaffold with per-Gaussian deformation and a stop-gradient scheme to decouple deformation gradients. It targets efficient, stable dynamic novel view synthesis without redundant primitive growth. The paper contributes to the active dynamic 3DGS area.

entry.title: GuidedAttention: Interpretable and Correctable Visual Attention for OOD-Robust Robot Manipulation via Imitation Learning

author.name: Masaki Murooka, Ryoichi Nakajo, Keisuke Shirai, Tomohiro Motoda, Hanbit Oh, Ryo Hanai, Yukiyasu Domae

entry.summary: Introduces GuidedAttention, a visuomotor imitation learning framework that predicts interpretable, human-correctable visual attention keypoints as an explicit intermediate representation conditioning a diffusion action policy, with corrections propagated by a tracking module. It improves out-of-distribution robustness and human oversight of end-to-end policies. The work targets interpretable, correctable manipulation.

entry.title: DecodeShare: Tracing the Shared Subspace of LLM Decode-Time Decisions

author.name: Zishan Shao, Lixun Zhang, Kangning Cui, Yixiao Wang, Ting Jiang, Hancheng Ye, Qinsi Wang, Zhixu Du, Yuzhe Fu, Fan Yang, Danyang Zhuo, Yiran Chen, Hai Helen Li

entry.summary: Proposes DecodeShare, a protocol that isolates a low-dimensional subspace shared across tasks in decode-time hidden states and shows via causal ablation that disrupting it harms decisions more than prefill or random subspaces. It links this shared subspace to activation-steering transferability.

entry.title: Tractable Hierarchical Control of Autoregressive Language Models

author.name: Max Scribner, Antonio Vergari, Vaishak Belle

entry.summary: Shows that satisfaction of any finite-duration LR(k) grammar can be enforced during autoregressive generation by distilling the LLM into a tractable probabilistic model that steers and masks tokens to guarantee valid output. It provides principled constrained decoding for structured languages like SQL and JSON.

entry.title: OPTScientist: Multi-Agent Discovery of Typed Optimizer Programs for Transformer Pretraining

author.name: Zhongzheng Li, Tiancan Feng, Wenhao Li, Qingsong Ran, Shikun Feng, Xiaoyuan Zhang, Yue Wang, Xiaoguang Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces OPTScientist, a theory-guided multi-agent framework that discovers transformer-pretraining optimizers within a typed domain-specific language, aiming to balance the flexibility of code search with the stability of parameterized families. It frames optimizer design as a constrained scientific search.

entry.title: MKEvolve: A Modular Multi-Agent Framework for Kernel Code Generation

author.name: Jason Yoo, Rajarshi Saha, Shaowei Zhu, Tao Yu, Wei Tang, Youngsuk Park

entry.summary: Introduces MKEvolve, a modular multi-agent framework that co-evolves the decomposition of complex PyTorch modules and LLM-generated kernels per submodule, refining via splitting/fusing and beam search. The resulting kernels are configurable, interpretable, and traceable compositions of verified subkernels.

entry.title: LeanFlow: A Case Study in Workflow-Driven Lean Autoformalization

author.name: Lazar Milikic, Simon Guilloud, Khanh Nguyen, Viktor Kuncak

entry.summary: Presents LeanFlow, an LLM agent system for translating math papers into buildable Lean projects, studied via case studies on two previously unformalized number-theory and measure-theory papers with model, workflow, and toolset ablations using existing frontier models. It reports full document-level formalization within a call budget.

entry.title: Is Deep Research Reliable? Misleading Knowledge Induces False Conclusions

author.name: Pengyu Zhu, Lijun Li, Longju Yang, Sen Su

entry.summary: Studies whether credible-but-false knowledge encountered by Deep Research agents propagates into false report conclusions, introducing MisKnow-Agent to construct and validate misleading knowledge with controllable authority and style, yielding 5,933 quality-controlled instances. It probes an underexplored reliability failure mode.

entry.title: SciExplore: Evaluating Autonomous Agents from Scientific Navigation to Information Integration

author.name: Yinhao Tang, Youqing Fang, Yanan Sun, Wenran Liu, Weiming Zhang, Bin Liu, Kuikun Liu, Wenwei Zhang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SciExplore, a benchmark of 103 expert-curated tasks across ten-plus disciplines evaluating scientific information-seeking and reasoning through database navigation, ambiguous literature retrieval, missing-reference completion, and cross-source knowledge synthesis. It probes progressively higher-order capabilities beyond static scientific QA.

entry.title: Identifying Good Rules for Efficient SAT Encodings of Single-Constant Multiplication Using Machine Learning

author.name: Chufeng Jiang (Graduate Center, The City University of New York), Neng-Fa Zhou (Graduate Center, The City University of New York)

entry.summary: Presents a neuro-symbolic framework that uses a graph neural network to predict promising operator types and prune search choices when generating SAT encodings for single-constant multiplication, an NP-hard hardware-design task. It accelerates encoding for large constants while preserving near-optimal quality.

entry.title: How Rules Represent Causal Knowledge: Causal Modeling with Probabilistic Logic Programming

author.name: Kilian Rueckschloss (Eberhard Karls Universitaet Tuebingen), Felix Weitkaemper (German University of Digital Science)

entry.summary: Transfers Pearl's causal framework into probabilistic logic programming, aligning programs with a non-temporal philosophical foundation where events are treated as simultaneous. It examines how rules can represent causal knowledge and support intervention prediction beyond acyclic Bayesian networks.

entry.title: Agentic Context Management: Solving Agent Memory and Cost by Treating Them as Lifecycle and Architecture Problems

author.name: Gaurav Dadhich

entry.summary: Argues that production agent failures stem more from unmanaged reasoning context, such as ballooning histories and tool outputs, than from poor reasoning, and reframes memory as a lifecycle and architecture problem rather than mere storage and retrieval. It proposes actively deciding what to remember, extract, store, consolidate, and forget.

entry.title: RE-AD: Real-Time Requirement Adherence for Data Labeling

author.name: Siddarth Malreddy, Ishan Nigam, Akshay Arora, Nikhil Mittal, Subrat Sahu

entry.summary: Introduces RE-AD, a real-time requirement-adherence framework that uses LLMs to proactively validate crowd-sourced data-labeling quality by decomposing standard operating procedures into atomic rules and applying tiered validation. It reports an F1 of 0.749 on a synthetic benchmark and 82 percent annotator acceptance of flagged errors in production.

entry.title: CAMeR: Keyword-Gated Hybrid Activation for Adaptive Memory Retention in LLM Agents

author.name: Haowen Lai

entry.summary: Presents CAMeR, a memory-retention framework for LLM agents that combines keyword-gated hybrid activation using both word-level Jaccard and embedding cosine similarity with adaptive weight dynamics, reinforcing relevant memories while decaying others. It introduces CAMeR-Bench to evaluate multi-round memory retention.

entry.title: From a Word-Level Dictionary to Sentence-Level Semantics: Multilingual Grievance Labelling with Contextual Models

author.name: Lin Tian, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: This paper critiques word-level grievance lexicons used in threat assessment, showing that a five-language evaluation pool is nearly perfectly separated by the lexicon's own retrieval rule, inflating apparent accuracy. It argues for contextual sentence-level models that can distinguish asserted, quoted, negated, or condemned uses of grievance terms.

entry.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education

author.name: Qian Wu, Xinrong Zhou, Zizhan Ma, Kai Chen, Zheyao Gao, Xun Lin, Hongqiu Wu, Longfei Gou, Yixiao Liu, Ann Sin Nga Lau, Qi Dou

entry.summary: MedGame transforms static clinical cases into executable storytelling games with a dual-engine design that synthesizes clinical storylines and orchestrates multimodal decision nodes, plus a 5,000-case benchmark. It targets decision-centered medical education beyond simple QA or single-turn feedback.

entry.title: Distribution-Alignment Bridge for Uncertainty-Aware Text-to-Video Retrieval

author.name: Kyeongmo Chae, Jihoon Lee, Sangtae Ahn

entry.summary: The Distribution-Alignment Bridge reframes text-to-video retrieval as aligning Gaussian-distributed embeddings rather than point matching, using a deterministic diffusion-inspired bridge to iteratively refine text distributions toward video distributions. It models modality-specific uncertainty with a distribution-aware contrastive loss.

entry.title: GeoThreat: Transferable Targeted Adversarial Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models for Remote Sensing Image Interpretation

author.name: Yimin Fu, Yuefeng Bai, Baicheng Pan, Zhunga Liu, Michael K. Ng

entry.summary: GeoThreat proposes transferable targeted adversarial attacks against large vision-language models for remote sensing interpretation, aiming to induce specified erroneous responses under black-box settings by exploiting joint local-global reasoning. It probes robustness of LVLMs in an underexplored geospatial domain.

entry.title: MVEI & EmObserver: Empowering MLLM-Oriented Visual Emotional Intelligence via Emotion Statement Judgement

author.name: Daiqing Wu, Dongbao Yang, Jiashu Yao, Hongrui Zhang, Can Ma, Yu Zhou, Sicheng Zhao

entry.summary: This work introduces an emotion-statement-judgement paradigm (MVEI and EmObserver) to systematically evaluate and improve the visual emotional intelligence of multimodal LLMs, addressing limited emotion taxonomies, ignored context, and labor-intensive annotation. It reframes affective image analysis to fit the open-ended, instruction-driven nature of MLLMs.

entry.title: Causal-AgentIR: Self-Evolving Causal Memory for Adaptive Image Restoration Agents

author.name: Hu Gao, Yulong Chen, Lizhuang Ma

entry.summary: Causal-AgentIR is a hierarchical multi-agent image-restoration framework with self-evolving causal memory that structures restoration knowledge to support accumulation, verification, revision, and forgetting over long-term experience. It moves beyond static tool descriptions and unstructured summaries used by prior restoration agents.

entry.title: T-STAR: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Spatio-Temporal Panoptic Scene Graph Generation in Satellite Video

author.name: Linlin Wang, Xue Yang, Zhihuang Zhou, Zhenyu Zhong, Ruiyuan Zhang, Yansheng Li

entry.summary: T-STAR is a large-scale benchmark introducing spatio-temporal panoptic scene graph generation in satellite video, requiring structured triplets with explicit temporal spans and identity-consistent instance masks. It targets high-level dynamic geospatial scene understanding where objects are small and relationships evolve over time.

entry.title: Stokes-Informed Diffusion for Robust Linear Polarization Estimation

author.name: Yidong Luo, Chenggong Li, Yuchao Feng, Boxin Shi, Junchao Zhang, Xin Yuan

entry.summary: GenPolar is a Stokes-informed diffusion framework grounded in the Mueller formalism that estimates linear polarization from a single RGB image, predicting Stokes components to stabilize angle-of-polarization estimates in weak-polarization regions. It removes the need for dedicated polarization hardware for applications like material detection and de-reflection.

entry.title: Boosting Robustness for All-Weather Self-Supervised Depth Estimation in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Mengshi Qi, Xiaoyang Bi, Xianlin Zhang, Huadong Ma

entry.summary: Proposes a self-training pipeline for all-weather self-supervised depth estimation in autonomous driving using unpaired real adverse-weather data via multi-teacher distillation and robust radar fusion. It addresses distorted pixel correspondences and sparse radar under bad weather. The work targets safety-critical perception robustness.

entry.title: GLAM-SLAM: Real-time Gaussian Large-scale Mapping via Flow Densification and Spatial Decomposition

author.name: Panagiotis Mermigkas, Argyris Manetas, Petros Maragos

entry.summary: Introduces GLAM-SLAM, a real-time decoupled Gaussian-splatting SLAM system for large-scale outdoor scenes using a feature-based frontend, sparse anchor-grid mapping, and flow-based densification to satisfy 3DGS initialization needs. It targets long-horizon scalability and memory limits of prior Gaussian SLAM. The work advances practical mapping.

entry.title: URF: A Unified Robot Control-Policy Framework for Stable Contact Aware Manipulation

author.name: Jiyou Shin, Youngjin Seo, Jaeseog Won, Sungwon Seo, Hyunjun Kim, Seokmin Yoon, Tuan Luong, Hyungpil Moon

entry.summary: Proposes the Unified Robot Control-Policy Framework, which connects compliant action prediction with unified impedance-admittance control by predicting a virtual target, stiffness matrix, and impedance-admittance switch ratio from multimodal observations. It addresses instability arising when learned policies are executed by a separate low-level controller in rigid contact. The work integrates policy and control for contact-rich tasks.

entry.title: Evaluating and Guarding Citation Faithfulness in Agentic Scientific Synthesis

author.name: Taewan Goo, Junsik Kim, Kyulhee Han, GwonYul Jo, Jong-Soo Kim, Tae-Hyung Kim

entry.summary: Audits the reliability of citation-faithfulness verifiers used by agentic scientific-synthesis systems like OpenScholar and PaperQA2, showing measured unsupported-citation rates swing from about 3% to 18% based purely on verifier strictness and that verifiers disagree on which citations to flag. It argues cross-paper comparison is invalid without a named verifier and protocol.

entry.title: Delivery, Not Storage: Cue-Anchored Working Memory as a Harness Property for Coding Agents

author.name: Swapnanil Saha

entry.summary: A single-author theory paper proposing that coding agents need a second, involuntary memory tier of situationally-cued operational facts, distinct from deliberately authored document memory. It argues this incidental memory should be a harness property rather than left to agent choice.

entry.title: HiMe: Real-Time Self-Hosted Personal Agent Platform for Health Insights with Wearable Devices

author.name: Wei Liu, Siya Qi, Linhai Zhang, Lorainne Tudor Car, Yulan He

entry.summary: Introduces HiMe, a locally deployable, privacy-first personal health agent platform that processes real-time wearable data across many devices with the database treated as a first-class component. It targets adaptive, in-context health insights while keeping personal data local.

entry.title: From Attention to Frequency: Integration of Vision Transformer and FFT-ReLU for Enhanced Image Deblurring

author.name: Syed Mumtahin Mahmud, Mahdi Mohd Hossain Noki, Prothito Shovon Majumder, Abdul Mohaimen Al Radi, Md. Haider Ali, Md. Mosaddek Khan

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-domain image-deblurring architecture that unifies a Vision Transformer backbone with an FFT-ReLU frequency-domain module, bridging spatial attention and frequency sparsity to suppress blur artifacts while preserving detail. Experiments on benchmark datasets show improved deblurring, especially on complex or high-resolution blur.

entry.title: The Storyteller in the Model: Narrative Pattern Inheritance, Escalation Dynamics, and Alignment Governance in LLMs

author.name: Adam Rigby, Raz Saremi, Azadeh Sohrabinejad, Mehdi Rahimi

entry.summary: Considers whether narrative conventions in human-authored training text, such as protagonist and antagonist archetypes and tension-resolution arcs, are absorbed by LLMs and later surface as adversarial or escalating behaviors over extended interactions. It synthesizes recent empirical alignment studies through a systematic literature review and cross-paper analysis.

entry.title: An Evaluation Framework for Structured Audio Captions Validated by Controlled Perturbations

author.name: Liang-Yuan Wu, Sripathi Sridhar, Mark Cartwright, Magdalena Fuentes

entry.summary: This work proposes a multi-axis evaluation framework for structured audio captions, assessing tag-sets, descriptions, logical reasoning, numeric measurements, and spectral profiles, validated via controlled perturbations. It combines LLM judges with targeted metrics to overcome the limits of flat caption metrics.

entry.title: RECO: Region-Aware Compensation for Extrinsic Perturbations in Roadside 3D Detection

author.name: Junsheng Du, Zhaocheng He, Yuhuan Lu

entry.summary: RECO is a region-aware framework that compensates for camera extrinsic perturbations in roadside 3D detection by predicting piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets partitioned into near and far regions. It mitigates the projective amplification of small extrinsic errors that degrade localization.

entry.title: ProCap: Prominence-guided Object Rectification for Faithful and Comprehensive Video Captioning

author.name: Debjyoti Das Adhikary, Aritra Hazra, Partha Pratim Chakrabarti

entry.summary: ProCap is a training-free, prominence-aware iterative post-hoc rectification framework for video captioning that ranks detected objects by saliency, temporal persistence, and relational dynamics before refining captions. It improves faithfulness and comprehensiveness without retraining the underlying model.

entry.title: Achieving Text-based Person Retrieval with Any Granularity

author.name: Jialong Zuo, Hanyu Zhou, Dongyue Wu, Yongtai Deng, Mengdan Tan, Nong Sang, Changxin Gao, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: This paper introduces text-based person retrieval at any query granularity, formalizing a five-level granularity spectrum, building a multi-grained dataset via an annotation engine, and proposing a holistic evaluation benchmark with cross-identity labels. It addresses the real-world uncertainty of how detailed a text query may be.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning Model for Cross-Modality Super-Resolution in Fluorescence Microscopy

author.name: Mohammad Soltaninezhad, Elena Corbetta, Francisco Paez Larios, Paul M. Jordan, Oliver Werz, Christian Eggeling, Thomas Bocklitz

entry.summary: This paper presents a physics-informed GAN for confocal-to-STED super-resolution fluorescence microscopy that incorporates microscope point-spread-function information into the training objective to keep outputs consistent with optical image formation. It reduces phototoxicity and instrumentation demands while avoiding physically implausible reconstructions.

entry.title: DAPM: UAV Monocular Depth Estimation from Any Height, Pitch, Roll and FOV

author.name: Tong Ling, Wenhui Diao, Yingchao Feng, Hanbo Bi, Zhongyan Hou, Xian Sun

entry.summary: Presents DAPM, a monocular depth estimation approach for UAVs that explicitly models varying height, pitch, roll, and field of view via a geometric analysis relating viewing angle to view distance. It aims to generalize across the diverse camera poses and depth scales in aerial scenes. It is a targeted robotics-perception contribution.

entry.title: Search Hardness-Aware LLM-Based Problem Formulation for Expensive Simulation-Driven Design

author.name: Yuchen Li, Handing Wang, Bing Xue, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SHA-PF, a search-hardness-aware LLM-based problem formulation framework for expensive simulation-driven engineering design that considers whether generated formulations induce an efficient search landscape, not just design-intent alignment. It integrates LLM formulation with optimization efficiency. The work links language models to black-box optimization.

entry.title: A Real-Time Generalized Nash Equilibrium Framework for Interaction-Aware Autonomous Driving in Mixed Traffic

author.name: Nouhed Naidja (L2S), Mohamed-Cherif Rahal (L2S), Steve Pechberti (L2S), St\'ephane Font (L2S), Guillaume Sandou (L2S), Marc Revilloud

entry.summary: Formulates interaction-aware autonomous driving in mixed traffic as a Generalized Nash Equilibrium Problem that explicitly models shared safety and geometric constraints linking the AV's feasibility to the opponent's actions, solved in real time via a Particle Swarm Optimization solver. It contrasts with decoupled optimization approaches. The work targets game-theoretic decision-making.

entry.title: PersonaTrail: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents through Browsing Trails

author.name: Seungbin Yang, Chaewoon Ki, Dohyun Lee, Jaegul Choo, ChaeHun Park

entry.summary: Introduces PersonaTrail, a benchmark for personalized web agents that must infer underspecified user intent from realistic raw browsing histories in a managed open-web environment. It evaluates preference inference and recall of past browsing sessions, which prior benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: Directional Hallucinations: Ideological Drift in News-Grounded LLM Question Answering

author.name: Chendi Wang, Liam Cunningham, Tom Yishay, Jieying Chen

entry.summary: Uses hallucinations in document-grounded political QA as diagnostic signals of ideological drift, analyzing over 21,000 expert-labeled left/center/right articles across several open and proprietary LLMs. It measures directional distortions in high-stakes election-adjacent settings.

entry.title: FlowEdit: Information-Theoretic Control of LLM Reasoning Flows for Ill-posed Problems Involving Conflicts

author.name: Sizhe Tang, Guangyu Jiang, Yu Li, Rongqian Chen, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis, Tian Lan

entry.summary: Proposes FlowEdit, an information-theoretic framework for handling ill-posed reasoning problems with conflicting or incompatible conditions by making hidden conflicts explicit, maintaining competing hypotheses, and generating alternatives in a single pass. It targets limitations of next-token prediction for conflict reasoning.

entry.title: ConfidenceBench: Evaluating Confidence Calibration in Large Language Models

author.name: Matthew ffrench-Constant, Daniel Yang, Xinmeng Huang, Sanyam Kapoor

entry.summary: Introduces ConfidenceBench, a calibration benchmark evaluating verbalized confidence in 15 frontier LLMs using the Brier proper scoring rule over 200 private multiple-choice questions across spatial reasoning, high-precision math, word lookup, and unknowable categories. It requires no logit access, working for closed and open models.

entry.title: DynamicMCPBench: A Trace-Grounded, Effect-Scored Benchmark for LLM Agents over Live MCP Servers

author.name: Jerzy Kami\'nski, Ilya Galyukshev, Artem Kuznetsov, Sergey Chuprin, Kirill Redko, Aidar Shumbalov, Anna Kalyuzhnaya

entry.summary: Presents DynamicMCPBench, a reusable framework that runs agents over live, stateful Model Context Protocol servers, generating realistic goals, recording successful trajectories, distilling them into path-agnostic effect checkpoints, and scoring by effects rather than fixed ground-truth tool lists. It addresses fragility of static MCP benchmarks.

entry.title: CMI-Mem: Toward Generalizable Long-Term Memory Management via CMI-Augmented Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yubo Wang, Qiuyu Zhao, Zenghui Sun, Shichao Dong, Jinsong Lan, Xiaoyong Zhu, Haoyang Li, Bo Zheng, Lei Chen

entry.summary: Proposes CMI-Mem, a lightweight RL-trained memory-manager model whose hybrid reward combines downstream QA correctness with intrinsic Conditional Mutual Information, valuing new conversational inputs relative to current memory without conditioning on a sampled query. It aims for more generalizable long-term memory management.

entry.title: ArbiGraph: Arbitrarily Scalable Verifiable Task Graphs for Evaluating Context Management

author.name: Pavel Golikov, Evgenii Opryshko, Gennady Pekhimenko, Mark C. Jeffrey

entry.summary: Introduces ArbiGraph, a benchmark generator that composes tasks into typed, arbitrarily scalable verifiable task graphs to test whether tool-assisted agents can retain, update, compose, and discard context across extended workflows. It enables controllable length, dependency structure, and distractors with exact automatic verification, evaluated with a Qwen3.5-27B agent.

entry.title: Bound-Founded Semantics for Answer Set Programming with Difference Constraints: Preliminary Report

author.name: Pedro Cabalar (University of A Corunna, Spain), Jorge Fandinno (University of Nebraska at Omaha, USA), Nicolas R\"uhling (University of Potsdam, Germany), Torsten Schaub (University of Potsdam, Germany, Potassco Solutions, Germany), Sebastian Schellhorn (University of Potsdam, Germany), Philipp Wanko (University of Potsdam, Germany, Potassco Solutions, Germany)

entry.summary: Introduces a many-sorted Bound-founded Logic of Here-and-There to give a unified logical foundation for Answer Set Programming extended with linear and difference constraints. It formalizes foundedness for numeric variables and characterizes semantics such as clingo[DL].

entry.title: Logic Programming Semantics for Causal Processes

author.name: Felix Weitk\"amper

entry.summary: Investigates the relationship between logic-programming semantics and the eventual states of causal processes, showing stable models of positive programs correspond to undisturbed processes from a neutral state while supported models describe states reachable from arbitrary starts. It adds a temporal, life-sciences-motivated perspective to stable versus supported model semantics.

entry.title: Logical Regression for Planning with Axioms

author.name: Connor Little, Christian Muise
